value.deviceOwnership:
DEVICES ARE AN UNNUMBERED SCREEN GROUP ON SURF-DOH, PINNED TO MOD-DOH-13 BY THE WORKFLOW CATALOGUE ONLY. SLICE 4 SHOULD BUILD IT, UNDER A NAMED OPEN DECISION.

(1) No MOD-DOH module is named for devices, and none silently owns one. The canonical §4.1.3 inventory of all nineteen DOH modules is enumerated in prose at L2436 (Band A: modules 1-13; Band B: 14-19) — no device module. Confirmed as 19 canonical DOH modules at L1568 and L1606, and by registries/generated/source-reconciliation.json (Modules row: 'DOH 19 (§4.1.3)').

(2) The screen is unnumbered and uncatalogued. The string `SCR-DOH-DEVICES` occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the entire frozen source — L67861, inside storyboard `SB-009-01`: 'Delivery Operations Hub, screen SCR-DOH-DEVICES Device enrollment: panel fields are device identifier, platform, device mode of Shared or Personal set at enrollment, location binding, application version against the floor, enrollment date, last seen, sync health, storage-pressure indicator and retire control.' It does NOT appear in registries/raw/identifier-index.json at all (that index carries SCR-DOH-001..026, SCR-DOH-01..23, SCR-DOH-ANOM/AUD/BANNER/PAH/QCAL/ROLE/... — no SCR-DOH-DEVICES). It is absent from BOTH numbered DOH screen catalogues: the 23-row table at L48093-48117 (SCR-DOH-01..23) and the 26-row table at L26049-26076 (SCR-DOH-001..026). Second uncatalogued appearance: `SB-SEC-005-S1` 'Delivery Operations Hub device inventory' at L103830, carrying the control 'Mark device lost / Request wipe' (Tenant Admin; 'Tenant-side state plus a wipe request routed to the platform team; wipes nothing itself').

(3) The workflow catalogue DOES assign an owner, and it is MOD-DOH-13. L53085: 'Enrolling a device into the tenant's fleet — WF-DVC-001 · Surface: Delivery Operations Hub · Module MOD-DOH-13'. L53118: 'Reassigning a device to another Area or worker group — WF-DVC-002 · Surface: Delivery Operations Hub · Module MOD-DOH-13'. L53150: 'Handling a lost device — WF-DVC-003 · Surfaces: Delivery Operations Hub and Super Admin platform console · Modules MOD-DOH-13, MOD-SA-13'. Routing table at L53076-53081. WF-DVC-004 (stolen), WF-DVC-005 (suspend), WF-DVC-006 (wipe) are Super Admin console / MOD-SA-13 only (L53189, L53224, L53257) — NOT slice 4.

(4) THIS CONTRADICTS MOD-DOH-13's OWN MODULE CARD. The card at L29178-29252 gives Purpose 'Make every platform-side access to a tenant's workspace visible to that tenant', Objects affected 'A filtered projection of OBJ-DOH-AUDIT; no new operational object' (L29187), and exactly three features — FEAT-DOH-13-1 Platform Access History, FEAT-DOH-13-2 Support-session transparency, FEAT-DOH-13-3 Announcements (L29240-29250). Zero device content. The catalogue row at L47264 agrees with the card (FEAT-DOH-1301/1302/1303 = access history, support banner, announcements). So the device screens have a workflow owner but no feature, no sub-feature, no functionality identifier and no acceptance criterion inside any module card. FINDING: the source is self-contradictory about MOD-DOH-13's remit.

(5) THE SOURCE ALSO CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON WHETHER THE CONTROL EXISTS AT ALL. Tenant-self-service side: §8.13.4 'The enrollment split — Tenant self-service enrolment within platform policy; the console keeps policy, telemetry and wipe authority' (L4715); 'a Tenant Admin enrolls their own tablets through the Delivery Operations Hub surface, within platform policy' (L18252, restated L45472, L53039, L8458); WF-DVC-001 happy path step 1 'Tenant Admin opens device enrollment' (L53089); AC-WF-DVC-001-01 'Enrollment is tenant-self-service and never a console write into tenant data' (L53099); MOD-SA-13's own role matrix row 'Enroll a device | Explicitly prohibited [x4 platform roles] | Allowed — enrollment is tenant-self-service within platform policy' (L45543); OBJ-034 Device enrollment 'Owning surface · system of record: Delivery Operations Hub for the act' (L8477). Platform-only side: the day-zero workspace storyboard at L61357 lists under Disabled actions 'Enrol a device — disabled with "Device enrolment is performed by the platform team from the Super Admin platform console"'; and §7.5.2 states device enrollment and lifecycle are Super Admin's (cited at L8459).

(6) THE BLUEPRINT ITSELF RAISES THIS AS AN UNRESOLVED CLIENT DECISION. `DEC-DEVOWN-001`, `Client Decision Required`, raised at L8459 on OBJ-033 Device: '§7.5.2 states that device enrollment and lifecycle are Super Admin's, while §8.13.4 states that enrollment operations are tenant self-service with the console keeping the policy layer, cross-tenant telemetry, and wipe authority. Both readings are preserved; this chapter splits the object's authority explicitly rather than choosing.' Restated L8472, L8491, and in the object-ownership table at L10324. There is NO adopted working position — the decisions extract records adopted_working_position: null at both L8459 and L10324. DEC-DEVOWN-001 is NOT in the decision canon list at L4552 (which names DEC-CAP-001, DEC-SYNC-001, DEC-STORE-001, DEC-WIPE-001, DEC-DEVICE-001, DEC-SCAN-001, DEC-UNIT-001) — it exists at only three lines in the whole source.

RECOMMENDATION FOR SLICE 4: build the device screen group under MOD-DOH-13, scoped to what SURF-DOH is unambiguously granted — enrol (WF-DVC-001), reassign (WF-DVC-002), retire (retire control, L67861), and mark-lost-plus-request-wipe (L103830, which explicitly 'wipes nothing itself'). Do NOT build suspend or wipe: WF-DVC-005 and WF-DVC-006 are MOD-SA-13, and wipe is a critical-class root-approved action (L45508, L107423). Ship it as an unnumbered screen group with a placeholder identifier, NOT as a numbered SCR-DOH-NN, because minting a number would invent a catalogue row the source does not have. Two open decisions block hardening: DEC-DEVOWN-001 (who may enrol) and DEC-DEVLOST-001, whose impact is recorded as 'Blocks WF-DVC-001 to WF-DVC-006' (L56662) and which has no lost/stolen classification in the source at all (L53160).
openScopeQuestions: DEC-DEVOWN-001 (L8459, L8472, L8491, L10324) is Client Decision Required with adopted_working_position NULL. Until it lands, slice 4 cannot know whether the Tenant Admin may enrol a device at all. §8.13.4 and MOD-SA-13's own role matrix (L45543) say yes; §7.5.2 and the day-zero storyboard at L61357 say no. Build behind a feature flag or get the decision before hardening.

DEC-DEVLOST-001 impact is recorded as 'Blocks WF-DVC-001 to WF-DVC-006' (L56662) — i.e. the whole device family including the two workflows slice 4 would build. The source has no lost/stolen classification at all (L53160). Confirm whether 'blocks' means design-blocking or acceptance-blocking before committing the mark-lost control at L103830.

MOD-DOH-13's module card (L29178-29252) omits both the tenant administration area and the device screens, yet WF-TEN-003 (L52469) and WF-DVC-001/002/003 (L53085, L53118, L53150) assign both to it. Which is authoritative — the module card or the workflow catalogue? Slice 4's module boundary for MOD-DOH-13 differs by roughly a factor of three depending on the answer.

THE TENANT ADMINISTRATION AREA HAS THREE DIFFERENT STATED OWNERS. WF-TEN-003 says 'Module MOD-DOH-13, tenant administration area (Part IX)' (L52469). Screen catalogue A says SCR-DOH-23 Tenant administration area is served by 'Part IX settings register, MOD-DOH-17' (L48117). Screen catalogue B says SCR-DOH-026 Tenant administration settings register is 'MOD-DOH-01 and cross-module' (L26076). It is confirmed to be a screen group and not a surface (L1598; AC-PROD-040 at L1614). MOD-DOH-02 depends on it for hierarchy depth and MOD-DOH-04 for gate posture and clearance duration (L27098, L27451 cards), so slice 4 must build it — but the owning module is unresolved.

TWO INCOMPATIBLE DOH SCREEN CATALOGUES EXIST AND THE SAME IDENTIFIER MEANS DIFFERENT SCREENS IN EACH. L48093-48117 numbers SCR-DOH-01..23; L26049-26076 numbers SCR-DOH-001..026. They are not a superset relationship: e.g. SCR-DOH-13 is 'Run schedule board' (L48107) while SCR-DOH-013 is 'Run schedule, today plus 7 days' (L26061), and catalogue A has a Sign-in screen (SCR-DOH-01, L48095) that catalogue B has no row for. Slice 4 must be told which catalogue is canonical before any screen identifier is coded.

MOD-DOH-12 scope split. FEAT-DOH-1201 single sign-on (L47260) versus MOD-DOH-09's FEAT-DOH-0903 two-track login (L47251) — the SSO connection record and the login track are in different modules, and MOD-DOH-09's card names MOD-DOH-12 as a dependency (L28503). Confirm slice 4 takes FEAT-DOH-1201 only and defers FEAT-DOH-1202/1203/1204.

DATA HAZARD IN THE SOURCE: FEAT-DOH-0903 is labelled 'Two-track login' at L47251 but 'gate-posture setting' at L16481. One of the two is wrong. Do not key slice-4 work off L16481's feature labels without checking them against L47249-47252.

MOD-DOH-19 Parts Registry is the genuine borderline call. It is tenant master data administered in the tenant administration area (L22025, 'Part IX, §4.3.6' at L22413 condition C27), which argues for 'tenant setup'; but every consumer named on its card is outside slice 4 — Studio authoring, Frontline package references, and MOD-DOH-06 genealogy (L30051). Excluded here. Confirm with the build-order owner.

COUNT SCOPE WARNING for whoever consumes this. The 19 in 'MOD-DOH-01..19' is the canonical §4.1.3 module inventory (L2436, L1568, L1606), not an extracted identifier count. The extraction under registries/raw/extract/ yields 81-13 repeated MOD-DOH-* entries across the 36 chunks (e.g. MOD-DOH-01 appears 13 times, MOD-DOH-15 nine times) — those are restatement occurrences, not modules. registries/generated/source-reconciliation.json keeps three distinct module scopes apart (81 canonical / 82 unique MOD-* ID strings / 87 raw tokens) and resolves the +1 as MOD-SA-20, an alias-by-denial that must never be minted.

modules.name: Location Configuration
modules.purpose: MATCHED BY module_id — the extract carries 11 distinct `modules` entries with id MOD-DOH-02 (L2436, L3700, L11141, L22008, L25958, L27098, L47225, L52542, L60775, L75761, L98148, L116397), all surface SURF-DOH, all named Location Configuration. The authoritative purpose is the module identity card at L27098-L27114: 'Hold the tenant's physical structure as the anchor for timezone, shifts, Job binding, scoping and reporting drill-down.' Inputs (L27103): Site name, timezone, plain-text address and contact; Area name and parent Site; Location name, parent Area and optional required certification; hierarchy-depth setting. Outputs (L27104): the location tree; the Job binding target; the scope values for Site and Area permission scopes; the Active Locations count metered at Site level; archival cascade notifications. Dependencies (L27107): tenant state from MOD-DOH-01; hierarchy depth from the tenant administration area; Job bindings from MOD-DOH-05 (SLICE 6 — slice 4 must build the cascade's Job-enumeration seam as an interface, not a behaviour). Fallback identifiers (L27112): FB-DOH-WRITE-002 primary, FB-DOH-CORE-001 for reads, FB-DOH-NOTIF-004 for cascade notifications. Note the purpose text DRIFTS across the 11 entries — L2436 says only 'configuring the location hierarchy; timezone is anchored at Site', L98148 says 'Configuration only; no timing stated'. Use L27098 as the governing card. Roles_allowed also drifts: five entries list Tenant Admin alone, two (L22008, L27098) list Tenant Admin + Supervisor + Quality Manager + Read-only Auditor, two (L98148, L116397) list none. The L27098 permission matrix is the resolving authority.

Archiving a Site or Area auto-pauses every Job bound to it, notifies the Tenant Admin with the list, and prompts reassignment before archival completes; the cascade cannot silently strand a standing Job.

Re-parenting a Location (Cell) or changing hierarchy levels is blocked while in-flight Jobs exist; Area split, merge and re-parent are not supported at V1. Enforcement note: 'controls absent rather than disabled'.
The hierarchy is Site to Area (Line) to Location (Cell) to Job to Run, and it is a platform-wide data-model contract no surface may fork.
Archiving an Area auto-pauses every bound Job, notifies the Tenant Admin with the list, and prompts reassignment before archival completes. Enforcement: Area archival state machine.
A Site cannot be omitted while shifts exist, and the timezone is inherited by every Shift bound beneath it. Enforcement: Location hierarchy configuration. BINDS BOTH MODULES.

Area split, merge and re-parent are not supported at version 1; a structural re-parent is blocked while in-flight Jobs exist and archive-and-recreate is the sanctioned path. Enforcement: Location Configuration structural edit check.
Archiving a Site or Area auto-pauses every bound Job, notifies the Tenant Admin with the list and prompts reassignment before archival completes [SoW Fact §4.3.3].

Every tenant has at least one Site from the moment provisioning completes, because a default Site is auto-created there, and no configuration path removes the Site level. Verifying test TEST-51-12 asserts the default Site exists BEFORE any Tenant Admin signs in and that the Tenant Admin is prompted to rename it.

A tenant can never operate with no Site: a default Site exists from tenant provisioning, it is a real renameable Site record, and no configuration path removes the Site level — the adopted working position of DEC-SITE-001.

The Job anchor is stored as a node reference capable of holding ANY hierarchy level, and the picker exposes every level the tenant configured. SHARED GATE — the picker is MOD-DOH-05 (SLICE 6), but the node-reference storage contract constrains the MOD-DOH-02 data model and must be built in slice 4.

Soft suspension blocks creation of new Jobs, Workers, LOCATIONS, SHIFTS, parts, and all configuration edits, while recertification of existing workers deliberately stays open. Enforcement: Delivery Operations Hub write path. SHARED with MOD-DOH-01.
Archival is manual only at V1; auto-archival of stale entities is deferred beyond V1. No entity is auto-archived at V1.
No object in the platform create-read-update-archive matrix exposes a hard-delete verb to any role. PLATFORM-WIDE; binds this module's archive semantics.
Named-location provenance is expressed in the tenant's own hierarchy names and is never a coordinate and never used as a gate. Constrains what the hierarchy may be used for downstream.

Scope is limited to Tenant, Site and Area, three orthogonal dimensions held simultaneously; Location (Cell), Job and worker-level scoping are deferred beyond V1 and no rule may depend on them. Enforcement: Scope assignment validation (MOD-DOH-09) — but it caps what MOD-DOH-02's Cell level may be used for.

modules.name: Shift Management
modules.purpose: MATCHED BY module_id — the extract carries 12 distinct `modules` entries with id MOD-DOH-03 (L2436, L3705, L11141, L22009, L25959, L27272, L47228, L52542, L60776, L75761, L98149, L99408, L116397). The authoritative purpose is the module identity card at L27272-L27286: 'Define the tenant's working-time blocks as the anchor for metering, production dating and escalation resolution.' Business rule at L27266-L27268: the Shift is a first-class entity created, edited and archived by the Tenant Admin in the tenant administration area; it binds to an Area, inherits the Site timezone and carries its own digest delivery time; it anchors THREE platform mechanics — the Worker-Shift consumption meter, the production_date rule for runs crossing midnight, and on-shift escalation resolution. Run records denormalise shift_id. Inputs (L27279): Shift name, nominal start and end times, parent Site, bound Areas, digest delivery time. Dependencies (L27282): MOD-DOH-02 for the Site and its timezone; MOD-DOH-01 for the suspension write class; the digest service in MOD-DOH-10 (SLICE 10 — slice 4 owns the digest TIME field and the scheduler registration seam, not the digest assembly). Fallback identifiers (L27285): FB-DOH-WRITE-002 primary, FB-DOH-SCHED-010 for digest delivery, FB-DOH-NOTIF-004 for escalation delivery. NAMING DRIFT: the entry at L99408 names MOD-DOH-03 'Delivery Operations Hub digest module (Card SCHED-007)' with purpose 'Assembles one sectioned digest per Shift entity at that Shift's own delivery time' — a different module identity under the same id; see openQuestions. Roles_allowed drifts identically to MOD-DOH-02; the L27272 card uniquely adds Worker to the role list because Workers may view their own assigned shift (L27297).

openQuestions: BLOCKING — DEC-SHIFT-001 (Shift-to-Area cardinality) is OPEN and the source itself calls it 'Blocking for Delivery Operations Hub module 3' (L112952, L113034) and 'Shift Management module blocked' (L116264, L116590). Options on the record: A — Shift to many Areas, Area to many Shifts, no overlap permitted on the same Area (recommended); B — Shift to many Areas, Area to exactly one Shift at a time; C — Shift to exactly one Area. Owner: the client's product owner; a Phase 0 exit item (L114767, L116445, L116509). MOD-DOH-03 CANNOT BE FULLY BUILT IN SLICE 4 UNTIL THIS IS RATIFIED. The proposed mitigation is on the record at L116590: 'The Shift entity with Site binding and timezone inheritance; DEFER AREA CARDINALITY.'

CONTRADICTION — the MOD-DOH-03 module deep-dive at L27272-L27410 never mentions DEC-SHIFT-001 anywhere. It states flatly 'A Shift binds to an Area' (L27266), 'She binds the Shift to one or more Areas' (L27302), 'Bind a Shift to one or more Areas' (FUNC-DOH-03-1.2.1, L27349) and 'Bind a Shift to Areas — Allowed' (L27294), i.e. it silently adopts a many-Areas reading. DEC-SHIFT-001 appears at only 10 line locations in the whole blueprint (L112897, L112910, L112952, L113034, L114767, L114841, L115447, L116264, L116445, L116509, L116590), all of them outside the module chapter. An implementer reading only §19.5 would build cardinality without knowing it is contested.

CONTRADICTION — DEC-SHIFT-001 is absent from registries/generated/source-reconciliation.json entirely (zero occurrences of the string in that file), including from its residual_contradictions list, which does carry DEC-SITE-001, DEC-AREA-001, DEC-PLUS-001, DEC-SUBAUTH-001 and DEC-QMNONE-001. The reconciliation artefact therefore under-reports the single blocking decision for MOD-DOH-03.

HARD GATE MISSING FROM THE MODULE CHAPTER — AC-51-13 (L113055): 'The platform refuses to create two Shifts with overlapping times bound to the same Area, stating the rule', enforcement 'DOH module 3 validation', verified by TEST-51-13. This overlap prohibition is stated NOWHERE in §19.5 (L27272-L27410) — not in the permission matrix, not in the features list, not in the nine acceptance criteria AC-DOH-03-1 through AC-DOH-03-6 (L27387-L27392), and not in the ten tests. It is also the substance of DEC-SHIFT-001 Option A, so it is simultaneously an undecided option and an asserted acceptance criterion. Slice 4 must resolve which it is before writing the validator.

HARD GATE IN PROSE ONLY — 'a shift may not span Sites' (L72144, step 3 of the eight-step shift-edit workflow). No business_rules entry in any of the 36 extract chunks carries this statement with is_hard_gate true, and it is absent from §19.5. It is nonetheless a structural constraint an implementer must enforce (the Shift's parent is a Site and the timezone is inherited from exactly one Site).

CONTRADICTION — the L27264 hard gate 'Editing a shift never retroactively re-stamps completed runs' is extracted at a LINE INSIDE the MOD-DOH-02 section range (L27098-L27271) while its enforcement_point names FUNC-DOH-03-1.1.2, a MOD-DOH-03 function. I attributed it to MOD-DOH-03 by enforcement_point. The same rule is extracted three more times with three different applies_to values and three different enforcement points: L3718 (applies_to 'SURF-DOH', enforcement 'MOD-DOH-03 Shift Management, §2.6'), L23878 (applies_to 'Shift entity', enforcement 'Shift Management'), L27264 (applies_to 'Shift edits', enforcement 'FUNC-DOH-03-1.1.2'). Four extractions of one rule; no canonical id — every instance is id 'unnumbered'.

CONTRADICTION IN MOD-DOH-02 EDIT SEMANTICS — the §19.4 permission matrix (L27119) and the module rule (L3945) both say name/address/contact edits are allowed AT ANY TIME and are 'ALWAYS allowed'. But the reconciliation row for FEAT-DOH-0202 'In-use location editing' at L47226 states FUNC-DOH-0202 as 'Refuse an edit that would retroactively re-stamp completed runs' — a refusal, not an always-allow, and phrased in the language of the SHIFT rule (§2.6) rather than the location rule (§4.3.2). Slice 4 must decide whether MOD-DOH-02 has a re-stamp refusal at all; §19.4 says it does not.

STATE VOCABULARY CONTRADICTION — five mutually incompatible state sets exist for the same Site/Area/Location objects: ['active','archived'] (L3915, L7796-L7834, L27106-L27107, L49419); ['created','updated','archived'] for OBJ-LOCATION (L22384); ['created','scope-pending','archived (soft archive)'] for Site in the WF-ORG-001 fallback ladder (L52555); ['Created','Unbound','Operational','Archiving','Archived'] for Area in the WF-ORG-002 state diagram (L52606); ['none','active'] for OBJ-SITE/OBJ-AREA/OBJ-CELL in the onboarding step table (L61465-L61466). The same fracture applies to Shift: ['active','archived'] (L3718, L27281), ['created','updated','archived'] (L22388), ['none','active'] (L61467). These are not synonyms — 'scope-pending', 'Unbound' and 'Archiving' are operationally distinct states with distinct downstream blocking behaviour (scope-pending excludes from role-assignment pickers; Unbound blocks Job creation; Archiving holds the cascade). Slice 4 must pick one machine per object and say so; I recommend the module identity cards (L27106-L27107, L27280-L27281) as governing and the WF-ORG diagrams as the operational elaboration, but the source does not rank them.

DIGEST SECTION COUNT CONTRADICTION — the digest sections are listed as three at L9228 ('expiring qualifications', 'review queue', "yesterday's exceptions") and as four at L68704 ('expiring certifications', 'review-queue aging', 'open anomalies', 'allocation position'). The MOD-DOH-03 fallback narrative at L27384 names a third set ('expiring qualifications in the worker records, review-queue ageing in the review queue, open anomalies in the Anomaly Register'). Digest content is MOD-DOH-10 (slice 10), but the per-shift digest TIME control in slice 4 must state what it schedules.

MODULE IDENTITY DRIFT — the extract entry at L99408 gives MOD-DOH-03 the name 'Delivery Operations Hub digest module (Card SCHED-007)' with purpose 'Assembles one sectioned digest per Shift entity at that Shift's own delivery time'. Every other MOD-DOH-03 entry names it 'Shift Management'. The digest ASSEMBLY belongs to MOD-DOH-10 (slice 10) per the MOD-DOH-03 dependency card at L27282. Slice 4 owns only the digest_delivery_time field and the scheduler registration seam; treat L99408 as an extraction misattribution, not as scope.

MOD-DOH-03 HAS ZERO EXTRACTED `controls` ENTRIES. Across all 36 chunks, 759 unique control entries, 653 of them carrying a module_id, NOT ONE is tagged MOD-DOH-03. MOD-DOH-02 has exactly three tagged entries (L27123, and two at L52542) plus three more matched by module NAME in a free-text module_id field (L67417 'Location configuration', L112905 and L112908 'Delivery Operations Hub module 2') and one matched by effect only (L71242, module_id 'unstated'). Every control I list for MOD-DOH-03, and eleven of the seventeen I list for MOD-DOH-02, are derived from the permission-matrix rows (L27117-L27127 and L27291-L27297) and the storyboards (L27217, L27377, L118001) — they are authoritative source statements of role authority, but the extraction pipeline did not classify them as controls. Do not treat any control count here as a canonical inventory.

NO WORKFLOW IN THE EXTRACT CARRIES A module_id FIELD AT ALL (0 of 725 entries). Every workflow-to-module assignment above is by one of three means, stated per workflow: (a) the workflow id embeds the module number — WF-DOH-02-CASCADE, WF-DOH-03-SHIFT; (b) the blueprint's own workflow header names the module — WF-ORG-001 and WF-ORG-002 say 'Module MOD-DOH-02' at L52555 and L52586, WF-ORG-003 says 'Module MOD-DOH-03' at L52623, and the MOD-DOH-02 module entry at L52542 lists WF-ORG-001 and WF-ORG-002 as its key_functions while the MOD-DOH-03 entry lists WF-ORG-003; (c) line proximity inside the module's chapter section (§19.4 = L27098-L27271, §19.5 = L27272-L27410). The four alternate-path and happy-path workflows at L27129, L27149, L27310, L27312 and L27314 were NOT extracted as workflow entries at all and are recovered by (c) alone.

DEC-SITE-001 IS AN ADOPTED WORKING POSITION, NOT RATIFIED — 21 extraction points (L2938, L3713, L6892, L11803, L22027, L23882, L27082, L30414, L39126, L47225, L49123, L52515, L56659, L60775, L61421, L66079, L72132, L75654, L112932, L117750, L119055) with SEVENTEEN different status strings, ranging from 'adopted working position, awaiting client ratification' to a bare 'open'. The adopted position (§4.3.1 mandatory Site, default Site auto-created at provisioning, renameable) is the STRICTER reading; §2.1 merely recommends it. Slice 4 builds against the adopted position but must keep the Site-optional path reachable by configuration rather than by code change (explicit instruction at L61533).

DEC-AREA-001 IS AN ADOPTED WORKING POSITION — 'one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth' supersedes 'one Area per Job' (L3713, L112909). This makes the Job anchor a NODE REFERENCE capable of holding any hierarchy level (AC-51-11, L113053). MOD-DOH-05 is slice 6, but the MOD-DOH-02 data model shipped in slice 4 must expose every level as an addressable anchor target or slice 6 cannot honour AC-51-11. The source explicitly notes a client reversal 'would narrow the picker rather than require a new one' (L112907).

DEC-NOSHIFT-001 IS CLIENT DECISION REQUIRED AND UNRESOLVED — the nobody-on-shift escalation fallback to the tenant's Quality Manager role (L27266, L27314, L27390) is a recommended default carried as an open drafting item in §3.9 and Part XII. The reconciliation artefact escalates this further as DEC-QMNONE-001: the fallback target is a ROLE which may itself be empty, so the 'escalation never resolves to no one' guarantee has a hole exactly where a Severity 1 needs a decider, and RISK-019 is the one register entry where residual risk equals inherent (High/High). Escalation delivery is MOD-DOH-10 (slice 10), but MOD-DOH-03 owns the on-shift ROSTER RESOLUTION (FUNC-DOH-03-2.2.1, L27352) that feeds it.

DEC-SCHED-001 IS OPEN AND AFFECTS THE PER-SHIFT DIGEST — the misfire policy (skip, run late, or merge) for a missed scheduled occurrence is undecided (L113045-L113052, L118008). AC-51-41 (L114527) requires every schedule definition to carry a DECLARED misfire policy, and AC-WF-ORG-003-03 (L52637) requires a missed digest to be recorded as missed rather than empty, but no policy is chosen. The §19.5 fallback narrative at L27384 asserts 'immediate backfill against the original due time, stamped with both its due time and its actual delivery time' — which is the run-late option — while L118008 states 'This blueprint does not choose.' Direct contradiction between the module chapter and the scheduled-work chapter.

MOD-DOH-02 HAS NO AI BEHAVIOUR AND MOD-DOH-03 HAS ALMOST NONE — both are explicitly 'None. No agent creates, edits, archives or proposes' (L27204, L27373). The one AI touchpoint is that the Shift Handoff Agent READS shift timing (default run time 30 minutes before shift end) but does not create, edit or archive a Shift; with all agents paused, shift management is fully functional and only the handoff brief becomes unavailable, rendering as unavailable rather than empty. Slice 4 needs no agent integration for either module.

NEITHER MODULE HAS AN OFFLINE WRITE PATH — every structural and Shift write control DISABLES offline and is NEVER QUEUED client-side, so reconnection requires no reconciliation of pending edits (L27206, L27208, L27367). The device-side consequence to honour is provenance immutability: a location renamed in the Hub while a device is offline does not retroactively rename provenance already captured, and captures arriving after a rename are reconciled against the current tree BY IDENTIFIER, NEVER BY NAME (L27208). Likewise captures arriving after a Shift edit retain the run's original denormalised shift_id (L27367). This is the single most important cross-slice contract MOD-DOH-02 and MOD-DOH-03 owe slice 6 and the Frontline surface.

COUNT SCOPE CAVEAT — the numbers in this map are counts of deduplicated EXTRACTION ENTRIES across 36 chunk files, not blueprint-declared inventories. For MOD-DOH-02: 11 module entries, 1 module-tagged control, 5 module-tagged screens, 2 module-tagged objects sets, 3 workflows with explicit module attribution. For MOD-DOH-03: 12 module entries, 0 module-tagged controls, 4 module-tagged screens, 1 object, 2 workflows with explicit module attribution. The blueprint states no per-module totals for any of these kinds, so no figure here should be treated as complete; the module chapters (§19.4 at L27098-L27271 and §19.5 at L27272-L27410) are the only places where the source itself enumerates exhaustively, and everything I found outside them (AC-51-13, the no-span-Sites rule, the depth-declaration control, the cascade-completion control) demonstrates that those chapters are not exhaustive either.

hardGates.statement: Supervisor permission alone authorises worker-record changes — the audit trail, not a second approval, is the control. Self-attestation of qualifications is not permitted.
The qualification gate is the only configurable gate on the platform — the specification gates and the evaluation gate are hard and non-configurable.
Notify-only is the platform floor for this gate — no silent posture exists, and no tenant setting can weaken the gate below it.
Qualification expiry raises a four-stage alert at 14, 7, 1 and 0 days. Tenants may add earlier warnings; they may never remove or delay a stage.

At the moment of expiry, under the strict posture, re-assignment to runs requiring the expired certification is blocked. The worker may complete the entire current run. There is no grace period beyond it.

hardGates.id: unnumbered (enforcement_point: FUNC-DOH-04-3.1.3, server-side at grant time)
hardGates.statement: A second clearance in the same Area on the same shift, regardless of worker, routes to the Quality Manager; the escalation scope is deliberately Area-level, not per-worker.
Recertification: the new expiry must be after the previous expiry. Back-dating the issue date is allowed; the platform records both the certification date and the entry date.
Departure is a two-step flow: first reassign all active and upcoming runs, then archive the worker. Open step executions are closed as abandoned with the reason 'Worker departed.'
Re-employment reactivates the prior record — history intact — with a re-validation prompt asking which prior qualifications still apply; nothing is silently re-trusted.
A clearance lapses automatically at the end of the tenant-set duration and never converts into a qualification; a lapse returns the worker to Expired rather than Valid.

hardGates.id: unnumbered (enforcement_point: FB-DOH-IMPORT-007 invariants; applies_to bulk import / file upload)
hardGates.statement: An import is all-or-nothing per file at V1 so a half-imported worker list cannot exist. No row is silently skipped. No row is silently transformed.

hardGates.id: unnumbered (enforcement_point: Worker Lifecycle and Qualifications module; applies_to Qualification OBJ-031)
hardGates.statement: Qualifications are supervisor-entered with full audit and never self-attested; a worker can never enter or amend their own qualification.

hardGates.id: unnumbered (enforcement_point: tenant gate posture setting validated against the floor register)
hardGates.statement: The qualification gate is the only configurable gate on the platform, with strict blocking as the default and notify-only as the floor; no silent posture exists.
At expiry under strict posture the worker may complete the entire current run and the block applies only after that run ends, with no grace period beyond it.

A Supervisor clearance covers an expired certification only; a never-held qualification requires the Quality Manager; a second clearance in the same Area on the same shift, regardless of worker, routes to the Quality Manager.

Under soft suspension, master-data writes are blocked while operations continue in full and recertification of existing workers stays open. Under compliance suspension, all logins are blocked immediately, in-flight runs stop, and devices lock at next contact with the fixed worker-facing message.

The login is the credential, not the device: identity, qualifications, language preference and attribution travel with the worker onto any conformant device, and a shared tablet confers nothing by itself.
A blocked run parks and the worker continues with their other assigned runs; the parked run resumes when the clearance arrives.
A recertification whose new expiry does not postdate the old is refused.
A clearance lapses automatically at the tenant-set duration and returns the certification to expired, never to active.
A worker cannot produce, alter, or attest to their own qualification record on any surface.
No worker may enter, edit, or attest their own qualification.
The four warning stages at 14, 7, 1, and 0 days cannot be removed or delayed by any tenant setting.
A qualification state change reaches a device only over the command channel and is reported per device, never as an instant global truth.
Under the strict posture a worker completes the current run and is blocked from the next assignment requiring the expired certification.
Attribution follows the login, never the device.
The cached-credential window cannot exceed 72 hours under any tenant setting.
A recertification expiry must postdate the previous expiry.
A second clearance in the same Area on the same shift routes to the Quality Manager irrespective of which worker it concerns.
The 14, 7, 1 and 0 day warnings all fire and cannot be removed or delayed by any tenant setting.
At expiry under the strict posture, the current run may complete and the next assignment is blocked.
A never-held qualification requires Quality Manager authorisation.
A clearance lapses automatically at the end of its tenant-set duration and the block re-applies at the next gate evaluation.
No qualification may be entered by the worker who holds it.
A recertification expiry that does not postdate the previous expiry is refused with the rule stated; no partial record is created and the worker's existing qualification state stands unchanged.
A worker cannot enter or amend their own qualification on any surface; self-attestation is not permitted.
Qualification validation runs at assignment, at Run start, and at every screen carrying an override.
A worker may complete the current run at the moment of expiry and cannot be re-assigned to work requiring the expired certification; there is no grace period beyond it.
A recertification whose new expiry does not postdate the previous expiry is refused; back-dating the issue date is allowed with both the certification date and the entry date recorded.
A qualification gate never resolves in the worker's favour because a clearance notification was sent but not delivered; the gate never fails open.
A qualification expiry warning stage cannot be removed or delayed; earlier stages can be added.
No interface anywhere in the application permits a worker to override a qualification gate.
A clearance is applied only as a validated command and carries the tenant-defined duration uniformly, not per user.
Clearance expiry re-blocks at the next gate evaluation and never interrupts the step under way.
No on-device control permits any role to override a qualification gate.
No surface shows a clearance as effective before its command reaches applied on the device.
Soft suspension blocks creation of new Jobs, Workers, locations, shifts, parts, and all configuration edits, while recertification of existing workers deliberately stays open.
Soft suspension blocks exactly the enumerated master-data write classes and leaves exactly the enumerated operational classes open, including recertification of existing workers.

Cached credentials and qualifications are trusted offline within a bounded window: tenant-set, default approximately 24 hours, platform ceiling 72 hours; a tenant may shorten it, never exceed the ceiling.
A qualification clearance carries a tenant-defined duration; its expiry is enforced at the next gate evaluation and the platform does not yank a worker out of the step under way.
The clearance duration is set at tenant level and applies uniformly, deliberately not per-user.

Qualification-expiry warnings may be configured earlier than 14 / 7 / 1 / 0 days and never later.

Prohibition 2 — a schedule never grants. It may never grant a qualification, extend a clearance, or bypass action-time validation.
A schedule can never be the enforcement mechanism; a missed qualification warning never suppresses the qualification block itself.
No offline path grants a qualification clearance, performs a sign-off, or releases a lot hold.

openQuestions: BLOCKING FOR MOD-DOH-14 — DEC-SCHED-007 (line 117962) is open and its impact field says verbatim 'Blocking for the Qualification Calendar module'. Its question is 'What is the stop condition for critical re-notification, and what does the 60-day Qualification Calendar view read?' The read model of the Calendar is therefore UNSPECIFIED in the frozen source. Slice 4 cannot finalise the Calendar query without this. Note also that DEC-SCHED-007 is cited elsewhere for unrelated subjects (RTO/RPO of the control plane, retry and dead-letter limits, command validity periods — contradiction recorded at line 99889), so the identifier itself is overloaded.

MOD-DOH-14 projection strategy is undecided — DEC-SCHED-008 (line 98348): 'Are analytical projections computed at read time or materialised on a schedule?' Status open, adopted working position 'read-time computation preferred', impact 'Staleness versus performance for calendars, aging highlights and board aggregates'. But WF-QUAL-PLAN (117975) describes a SCHEDULED recompute whose terminal state is 'the calendar shows its computation time and is not presented as live', i.e. the materialised reading. The two are inconsistent. DEC-SCHED-008 is also overloaded — at 117964 and 119095 it is cited for the on-call escalation recipient question instead.

QUALIFICATION-ENTRY AUTHORITY FOR TENANT ADMIN IS DIRECTLY SELF-CONTRADICTORY, and it is the single highest-risk ambiguity in slice 4. Allowed: line 10345 'Allowed on Worker record and Qualification create, read, update, archive' (Tenant Admin); line 23624 Tenant Admin MAY 'enter worker qualifications'; line 52756 Tenant Admin MAY 'create a worker record, issue or reissue a credential, record or renew a qualification'; line 29345 'qualification entry is a Supervisor and Tenant Admin act'. Prohibited: line 33638 Tenant Admin MAY NOT 'Enter or amend a worker's certification record'. And the MOD-DOH-04 role-by-action matrix at 27470-27476 contains NO Tenant Admin row at all, only Supervisor, Worker and Quality Manager.

QUALITY MANAGER QUALIFICATION-ENTRY AUTHORITY IS ALSO CONTRADICTORY. Line 27476 (the MOD-DOH-04 matrix) says Quality Manager MAY NOT 'Enter a qualification' or 'Record a recertification'. Line 51387 says Quality Manager MAY 'record or renew a qualification'. Both are SURF-DOH statements about the same module.

MOD-DOH-04 roles_allowed differs in every restatement, and no restatement matches the role-by-action matrix. Recorded sets: [Supervisor, Tenant Admin] (2436, 11141, 60777, 99402); [Supervisor, QM, Tenant Admin, Worker] (3707); [Tenant Admin, Supervisor, QM, Read-only Auditor] (22010); [Supervisor, Tenant Admin, QM] (25960); [Tenant Admin, Supervisor, QM, Read-only Auditor, Worker] (27451); [Supervisor] alone (47231); [Supervisor, QM] (75884, 98150, 116397); [Tenant Admin, QM] (86602). The matrix at 27470-27476 covers only Supervisor, Worker, Quality Manager — Read-only Auditor and Tenant Admin, both named in the 27451 identity card, have no row.

Recorded sets: [Quality Manager] alone (2436, 11142, 19523, 25970, 47267, 60787, 75944); [Tenant Admin, Supervisor, QM, Read-only Auditor] (22020); [QM, Tenant Admin, Supervisor, Read-only Auditor] (29326); [QM, Tenant Admin, Supervisor] (52740); [QM, Supervisor] (98160); [Supervisor, Tenant Admin] — Quality Manager ABSENT (99412); empty array (116397). Two incompatible numbering schemes are in the frozen source: three-digit SCR-DOH-007 / -008 / -009 / -010 (lines 26057-26060) and two-digit SCR-DOH-07 / -08 / -09 (lines 48101-48103, confirmed in identifier-index.json). DEC-WKRVIEW-001 (line 23067, open) directly contradicts two rows of the MOD-DOH-04 matrix. Line 27472 grants the Worker 'View a worker record — own record only' and 'View own certification alerts — own certifications only' on SURF-DOH, but section 1.2 excludes Workers from Hub primary users and sections 5.18 and Part VII confine workers to SURF-FL. DEC-ANON-001 (open, carried unresolved at lines 2039, 8375, 19051, 26969, 44187) — whether worker personal-data anonymisation at 24 months stands under the platform's no-purge model. Adopted working position 'Presumed yes'. This governs the terminal state of OBJ-WORKER-IDENTITY, whose authoritative_owner_surface is recorded as SURF-SA (117355) even though the worker record it anonymises is SURF-DOH-owned. Anonymisation is described as 'the platform's one irreversible act'.

DEC-SCHED-011 (line 98701) records 'A delivery-channel contradiction affects qualification-expiry warnings and the per-shift digest', with the note that 'both readings preserved in the source'. The 14/7/1/0 warning delivery channel is therefore not determined. Related: DEC-DIGEST-001 (line 5273) — the per-shift digest section list differs, four sections in 4.9.4 including allocation position versus three in Part IX including 'yesterday's exceptions'; both lists include certification/qualification expiries, so MOD-DOH-14's digest section is affected.

DEC-AUDITSUP-001 (line 74178, open) — Supervisor audit read access 'is not stated anywhere in the source although Supervisors perform audited clearances, release requests, substitutions and cancellations'. Options span 'no access' to 'read of the Supervisor's own actions only'. Since MOD-DOH-04's stated control is the audit trail rather than a second approval (27419), a Supervisor who cannot read the audit trail cannot verify the control that authorises their own writes. Companion DEC-AUDITQM-001 (same line) notes the Quality Manager likewise cannot read their own never-held clearance authorisations under the literal reading.

MODULE IDENTIFIERS ARE REUSED FOR DIFFERENT SUBJECTS. MOD-DOH-01 appears as 'Tenant Lifecycle and Tier Operations' (2436, 3895), as an 'onboarding role-mapping worksheet' (18024) and as 'tenant-state enforcement (Card SCHED-022)' (99432). MOD-DOH-04 itself appears once as 'Delivery Operations Hub qualification module (Card SCHED-004, SCHED-006)' (99402) and once with purpose 'Authoritative source of qualification records used for readiness cross-reference' (86602) — name-matching alone will over-collect. All MOD-DOH-04 and MOD-DOH-14 matches reported above were made by MODULE_ID where the id was present, which was every case; workflows, objects, business_rules and state_vocabularies carry NO module_id field at all and were matched by NAME plus LINE PROXIMITY to the module identity cards at 27451 and 29326 and to the module screen blocks at 26057-26060, 48101-48103 and 52740, and every such inference is marked in the entry.

MOD-DOH-14 HAS EXACTLY TWO WORKFLOWS in the whole extract (WF-DOH-14-CAL at 29352 and WF-QUAL-PLAN at 117975), ONE OBJECT (OBJ-QUAL-CALENDAR at 117944), ONE HARD GATE OF ITS OWN (29426), and NO STATE VOCABULARY. This is not an extraction gap — it is consistent with a no-write projection module. But it means the module's entire behavioural specification is: read MOD-DOH-04's qualification records over a fixed 60-day forward window, group and filter, link out. Everything else it might do is unstated.

THE CALENDAR'S ONLY STATED TEST BOUNDARY is TEST-DOH-14-N1 at line 29433: '5, 30, 59, 60 and 61 days out — first four appear, the fifth does not'. The 60-day boundary is therefore inclusive. No other Calendar test is recorded, and no test exists for the recompute cadence, the computation-time display, or Calendar unavailability.

MOD-DOH-04 BULK IMPORT HAS ONE RULE AND NO FAILURE CARD OF ITS OWN. The rule at 26707 is a hard gate ('all-or-nothing per file at V1', 'no row silently skipped', 'no row silently transformed') but its enforcement_point points at FB-DOH-IMPORT-007, and the only extracted FB-DOH-IMPORT-007 (line 30152) describes a bulk PARTS upload with a per-row per-column error report. There is no worker-import failure card, no stated row limit, and no stated template schema beyond 'canonical template only' (27470).

MOD-DOH-04 SPANS THE SLICE BOUNDARY IN TWO PLACES AND THE BLUEPRINT DOES NOT MARK IT. (a) Qualification validation is stated to run at THREE points — assignment, run start, and override-carrying screens (28214, AC-STU-114 at 33765, 68094, AC-ONB-070 at 75964, 61626). Assignment and run start are MOD-DOH-07 and MOD-DOH-06, i.e. slice 6. Slice 4 owns the record and the evaluator; two of three enforcement points land in slice 6. (b) WF-WKR-004 (52892) and WF-WKR-005 (52924) sit inside the MOD-DOH-04 screen block at 52740 by line proximity but their subject is Permissions, Roles and Access = MOD-DOH-09. Confirm the split before assigning them.

WF-QUAL-CLEAR (line 117490) omits SURF-DOH from surfaces_touched, listing only [SURF-CC, SURF-FL], while the same clearance path at 16657 (WF-CC-GRANT-CLEARANCE) and 27498 (WF-DOH-04-CLEARANCE) both include SURF-DOH. Similarly SB-020 lists [SURF-FL, SURF-CC] at line 61109 but [SURF-FL, SURF-CC, SURF-DOH] at line 64319 for the same storyboard. surfaces_touched is not reliable as a sole filter.

hardGates.statement: There is no payment integration, no invoicing and no pricing engine at any tier. Applies to all tiers.
No Delivery Operations Hub capability is tier-locked at V1. Custom Job Types, Service Type tags, single sign-on and retention are available uniformly across all tiers.
A tier upgrade is effective immediately and never resets consumed allocation. Enforcement point: tier change service.

Soft suspension blocks exactly the enumerated master-data write classes and leaves exactly the enumerated operational classes open, including recertification of existing workers. Enforcement point: write-class gating FUNC-DOH-01-2.1.1.
Compliance suspension blocks all logins immediately and delivers the fixed worker-facing message to devices at next contact, never before. Enforcement point: FUNC-DOH-01-2.1.3.
An upgrade never resets consumption.
A downgrade cannot take effect mid-cycle and queues where consumption does not fit.
Tier records carry no price metadata.
A Tenant Group is never rendered in any tenant-facing surface and carries no operational behaviour at V1. Enforcement point: tenant-facing endpoints return no group reference.

Under soft suspension, master-data writes are blocked while operations continue in full and recertification of existing workers stays open. Under compliance suspension, all logins are blocked immediately, in-flight runs stop, and devices lock at next contact with the fixed worker-facing message.
Under hard suspension every surface denies writes except the enumerated completion pipeline. Enforcement point: suspension state check, before role grant.

An action that cannot be audited does not happen. A partial write is never visible. A write is never queued client-side. Where tenant state cannot be determined, the stricter interpretation applies. Enforcement point: FB-DOH-WRITE-002 invariants; applies to master-data and configuration writes.

Soft suspension blocks creation of new Jobs, Workers, locations, shifts, parts, and all configuration edits, while recertification of existing workers deliberately stays open. Enforcement point: Delivery Operations Hub write path.

Hard suspension is read-only except the enumerated completion pipeline: no new runs, while in-flight runs complete, capture, sync, compute summaries and close, with mandatory notifications and audit continuing. Enforcement point: Delivery Operations Hub write path.
Compliance suspension blocks all logins immediately, stops in-flight runs, and locks devices at next contact with the fixed worker-facing message. Enforcement point: login path and command channel.

Suspension is a three-state machine drawn by data type: writes that grow or reshape the account's master data are blocked first while writes that operate the existing account continue as long as possible. Enforcement point: Delivery Operations Hub enforcement layer working from enumerated lists.

Under soft suspension master-data screens block writes while operational screens keep working; under hard suspension everything is read-only except the enumerated completion pipeline; under compliance suspension nobody gets in at all. Applies to Delivery Operations Hub screens.
Under STATE-06 the cause is always named — tenant hard suspension, an archived object, a role without write authority, or a support session; 'read-only' alone is never shown. Applies to all screens.
No Boolean blocked field exists on the tenant record; blocking is expressed through the three defined suspension states.
Every suspension-state transition writes tenant state history and is audited, and no transition exists that is not in the enumerated table.
A soft suspension can be lifted by a recorded operator action without any payment integration being present.
Recurrence generation creates no new runs for a hard-suspended tenant. (Slice-6 surface, slice-4 gate: module 01 owns the state this reads.)
Pilot conversion preserves the tenant identifier and requires no re-onboarding.
Downgrades never execute mid-cycle and carry a visible pending-downgrade status, queued behind consumption fit.

The usage ladder produces flags, never enforcement: 80 per cent banner, 100 per cent escalation, 100-125 per cent burst tolerance with burst entry recorded, above 125 per cent a flag opening a commercial conversation.
Export on archival is provided at no charge and archival does not execute until it has been provided. Enforcement point: archival execution screen — 'Skip the export' is disabled.
Onboarding is invitation-driven and there is no public self-signup at V1; pilot tenancies are invitation-only with no public free trial and are functionally identical to a paying tenant.
A per-tenant override is stored as a flag on the tenant record — visible and audited — and never as an edit to the tier record.

The compliance-suspension worker-facing message is fixed verbatim: 'Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved.' Enforcement point: device lock at next contact. (Rendered on SURF-FL, gated by module 01's state; two rival wordings exist — see open questions.)
A notification must never be the only mechanism enforcing a hold, a qualification, an authorisation, an approval, a suspension, or a device command; enforcement lives in the record and on the device.

Beyond the credential-trust window without contact, the device forces re-sync and blocks new work rather than trusting cached credentials or cached tenant state. Applies to user account, role grant, scope grant, qualification, tenant state.
Suspension by tenant state cannot be resumed from the scheduling console.

modules.name: Tenant View of Platform Administration
modules.purpose: MATCHED BY module_id (12 deduplicated module rows carry id MOD-DOH-13, at L2436, L11141, L14789, L22019, L25969, L29178, L47264, L52469, L60786, L75761, L98159, L99438, L116397). The fullest statement is L29178: 'Make every platform-side access to a tenant's workspace visible to that tenant, and give the tenant a control it can actually exercise', classified 'SoW Fact at 4.12 through 4.12.4, 8.15 and 8.16; identity card, session and announcement state names are Derived Clarification'. Other purpose statements: L2436 'Band A module giving the tenant a read-only view of platform administration affecting it'; L11141 and L47264 'Platform Access History, support-session banner with End-session control, platform announcements'; L14789 'Carries the tenant's Platform Access History listing every cross-tenant access event ever taken against the workspace'; L60786 adds 'agent pause state'; L116397 adds 'tenant settings'. The scope BOUNDARY is stated as a hard gate at L29172 (enforcement point AC-DOH-13-7): 'The Hub shows the tenant its own position, read-only — nothing more. No tier configuration, feature gate, pilot management, tenant-group management, impersonation control or usage administration is reachable from the Hub.' ROLES: L29178 lists Tenant Admin, Supervisor, Quality Manager, Read-only Auditor; L22019 the same four; L14789/L25969/L47264 list Tenant Admin + Read-only Auditor; L2436/L11141/L52469/L60786/L75761/L98159/L116397 list Tenant Admin only. The role rule at L29199 is broader than all of them: 'Any signed-in tenant web user' may end a support session from the banner at any time, with the scope condition that 'the control belongs to the tenant; deliberately available to any signed-in tenant web user rather than only to the Tenant Admin'; that same rule says no tenant user may dismiss or hide the banner while the session is open, post or edit a platform announcement, initiate or approve a compliance-emergency access, or prevent a platform-side access class from being recorded. FUNCTION DECOMPOSITION: the card at L29178 names 5 functions FUNC-DOH-13-1.1.1, 1.1.2, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 3.1.1. identifier-index confirms 3 features FEAT-DOH-13-1/2/3 (L29240, L29244, L29248), 3 sub-features SUB-DOH-13-1/2/3, 3 function groups FUNC-DOH-13-1/2/3, and a SECOND parallel numbering FEAT-DOH-1301/1302/1303 with SUB-DOH-1301..1303 and FUNC-DOH-1301..1303 at L47264-L47266; a third form FUNC-DOH-13010001 appears at L16963 and FUNC-TEN-017 at L22226/L22780. NO feature, sub-feature or function ROW was extracted in any chunk. identifier-index shows 7 acceptance criteria AC-DOH-13-1..7 at L29284-L29290 and 11 tests TEST-DOH-13-N1..N2, D1..D4, O1, F1..F2, R1..R2 at L29296-L29306 — ZERO of the 7 ACs and zero tests were extracted as rows; only AC-DOH-13-7 is reachable, indirectly, as the enforcement_point of the L29172 gate. KEY NUMERIC FACTS on the card: 3 platform-side access classes mirrored to the tenant (support sessions, compliance-emergency procedure, granted delivery-partner access) at L29166; support session time box default 2 hours, reason-required and ticket-linked, at L29168; compliance-emergency access requires 2 senior platform staff, dual-authorised, and is the only access class with write capability into tenant data, at L29172. FIXED BANNER STRING (hard gate, L23801): 'Platform support is viewing your workspace. Started [time]. Engineer [name]. End session.'

hardGates.statement: All three platform-side access classes appear in Platform Access History, mirrored into the tenant's own audit trail identically: support sessions, the compliance-emergency procedure, and the granted delivery-partner access class.
The tenant can terminate a support session from the banner at any time; every action in the session is logged to the tenant's audit trail. Support access is read-only at V1.

The Hub shows the tenant its own position, read-only — nothing more. No tier configuration, feature gate, pilot management, tenant-group management, impersonation control or usage administration is reachable from the Hub.

Every platform-side access event against a tenant appears in that tenant's own audit stream and in the tenant's Platform Access History screen. Enforcement point: mirroring obligation on all three access classes.
Every platform-side access event against a tenant appears in that tenant's Platform Access History and audit log, from the moment the session opens.
Platform Access History reads the same records rather than a separate view. Enforcement point: tenant-facing view construction.
Cross-tenant access events mirror into the affected tenant's own stream; the tenant-facing Platform Access History reads the same records rather than a separate summary. One audit truth per tenant.
All three access classes appear identically in the tenant's Platform Access History, and no filter or export can omit a class.

There are exactly three named access classes and only three: the normal support session, the compliance-emergency path, and the JBS access grant. No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console. (Restated at L4612, L9689, L23534, L54952, L64448, L70643, L72755.)

No tenant record is read while the tenant cannot see that it is being read; if the banner cannot render, the session is suspended and no further reads are served until the banner is confirmed visible. Enforcement point: banner heartbeat, session suspension.
No banner means no session: the session does not open, or terminates, if the banner cannot be shown — visibility is a precondition of the access rather than a decoration on it.
No read of tenant operational content occurs before the tenant banner is confirmed displayed and the session-open event is committed to the tenant's audit stream.
Banner text is fixed in the source: 'Platform support is viewing your workspace. Started [time]. Engineer [name]. End session.' Applies to all open access sessions on tenant-facing surfaces.

A persistent banner naming the engineer and start time renders to the tenant for the whole session, with a working End-session control. Enforcement point is a tenant UI rendering property, explicitly NOT the notification machinery.
Pressing End session terminates platform access immediately.

Tenant termination of a support session is immediate and unconditional; a failed termination is recorded, not hidden. Enforcement point: banner End-session control. (Restated as AC-UC-PSUP-08-01 at L58135.)
The tenant's End-session control terminates a support session immediately and the termination is audited.
Support access is reason-required, ticket-linked, time-boxed, tenant-visible and terminable; if the timer fails, the tenant's End-session control still closes it.
No in-place extension of a support session; overruns are recorded. Enforcement point: session expiry job plus the tenant banner as a second mechanism.

No write capability exists in a support session; the banner is present for the entire session with a working End-session control; sessions expire at the configured time box, default two hours; every action mirrors to the tenant's audit stream.

No write capability exists inside a normal support session for any account including the root — read-only without exception. (Restated at L9966, L16022, L18865, L23771, L48721, L57962, L104317 AC-SEC-802, L107884 AC-4871 'every mutating control is absent rather than disabled-with-a-tooltip', L112819 AC-51-09.)
An automatic post-session report is generated for the tenant on every close, including a close by time-box expiry. Applies to compliance-emergency session close.
The tenant automatically receives a post-session report after a compliance-emergency session; the control to suppress the tenant report does not exist.

No End-session control is offered for the compliance-emergency class, because an emergency access the tenant could terminate would not be an emergency access. Enforcement point: Delivery Operations Hub banner for emergency class; applies to Tenant Admin.
Band B actions auto-apply and are audited; every tenant-visible act mirrors — no unmirrored platform-side act against a tenant persists, because Platform Access History is a tenant right.
Every cross-tenant access event mirrors into the affected tenant's audit stream.
In-app banners cannot be muted by any tenant user. Applies to the announcements feature.
An in-app incident banner cannot be muted and displays for its defined duration. Applies to tenant surfaces.

No surface renders a role selector, an 'acting as' control, an 'acting as' banner, or any session-level role context. Applies to interface design across all five surfaces — the reason the module has no impersonation view.
No tenant role can authenticate to the Super Admin platform console under any configuration, including during a support session, a compliance-emergency session, or a JBS grant.
No observability view, alert, dashboard, or export in the platform console exposes record-level operational content outside a support session, the compliance-emergency path, or a JBS access grant.

openQuestions: MOD-DOH-13 HAS NO EXTRACTED ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. identifier-index.json lists AC-DOH-13-1 through AC-DOH-13-7 at L29284-L29290 and 11 tests TEST-DOH-13-N1/N2/D1-D4/O1/F1/F2/R1/R2 at L29296-L29306, but ZERO of them were captured as business_rules rows in any of the 36 chunks. Only AC-DOH-13-7 is reachable, and only indirectly, as the enforcement_point of the L29172 scope gate. Slice 4 cannot write acceptance tests for this module from the registry as it stands — the blueprint lines L29284-L29306 must be re-extracted.

MOD-DOH-01 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ARE 25 PERCENT CAPTURED. identifier-index lists AC-DOH-01-1..12 at L27039-L27050; only AC-DOH-01-2 (L27040), -5 (L27043) and -7 (L27045) exist as extracted rows. AC-DOH-01-1, -3, -4, -6, -8, -9, -10, -11, -12 and all 13 TEST-DOH-01-* rows (L27056-L27068) are line-numbers only. Count scope: 3 of 12 named ACs extracted, not 3 acceptance criteria in the blueprint.

NO FEATURE, SUB-FEATURE OR FUNCTION ROWS EXIST FOR EITHER MODULE. Both modules decompose into 3 features / 3 sub-features / 3 function groups per identifier-index (FEAT-DOH-01-1/2/3 at L26979/26988/26995; FEAT-DOH-13-1/2/3 at L29240/29244/29248), and MOD-DOH-01's card additionally names 12 FUNC-DOH-01-x.y.z identifiers and MOD-DOH-13's names 5 FUNC-DOH-13-x.y.z. Not one of those identifiers has a name, statement or behaviour recorded anywhere in the extract. The implementation team has function IDs with no function definitions.

TWO INCOMPATIBLE FEATURE NUMBERING SCHEMES COEXIST. FEAT-DOH-01-1/-2/-3 (L26979-L26995) and FEAT-DOH-0101/0102/0103 (L47222-L47224) both claim MOD-DOH-01; FEAT-DOH-13-1/-2/-3 (L29240-L29248) and FEAT-DOH-1301/1302/1303 (L47264-L47266) both claim MOD-DOH-13. Same for SUB-* and FUNC-*. The blueprint never states they are the same three features. Pick one scheme before writing any traceability matrix, and record which.

TWO INCOMPATIBLE SCREEN REGISTERS COEXIST, WITH A DANGEROUS COLLISION. Register A is SCR-DOH-001..026 (L26051-L26076); register B is SCR-DOH-01..23 (L48095-L48117). In register A, SCR-DOH-023 is Platform Access History (MOD-DOH-13). In register B, SCR-DOH-23 is the Tenant administration area (attributed to 'Part IX settings register, MOD-DOH-17') and Platform Access History is SCR-DOH-22. A build that treats SCR-DOH-23 and SCR-DOH-023 as one identifier will wire the tenant admin area to the platform access history. Also note SCR-DOH-BANNER-01 names the support-session banner at L14851 and the soft-suspension banner at L81540.

WHO OWNS THE TENANT ADMINISTRATION AREA IS UNRESOLVED ACROSS THREE MODULES. L52383 and L52469 assign it (and WF-TEN-003, WF-DVC-001, WF-DVC-002, device enrollment) to MOD-DOH-13; L26076 assigns SCR-DOH-026 'Tenant administration settings register' to 'MOD-DOH-01 and cross-module'; L48117 assigns SCR-DOH-23 'Tenant administration area' to MOD-DOH-17. This is the single largest scoping question in slice 4, because device enrollment and tenant configuration are explicitly in slice 4 while MOD-DOH-13's own scope gate (L29172) says the module is read-only and shows the tenant nothing but its own position. A read-only module cannot own device enrollment.

THE L52469 MODULE ROW CLAIMING MOD-DOH-13 CARRIES A DIFFERENT MODULE NAME. Its name field reads 'tenant administration area (Part IX)', not 'Tenant View of Platform Administration', and its purpose covers locations, shifts, roles, notification policy, qualification posture, severity bundles and device enrollment. Either the id is wrong on that row or the module has a second, undeclared scope. Treat WF-TEN-003, WF-DVC-001 and WF-DVC-002 as attributed-but-disputed rather than confirmed module-13 workflows.

MOD-DOH-01 AND MOD-DOH-13 ARE SWAPPED IN THE SCHEDULING CARDS. At L99430 a control tagged MOD-DOH-01 is the tenant's End-session control (a module-13 concern), and at L99438 a module row tagged MOD-DOH-13 is 'Delivery Operations Hub tenant usage view (Card SCHED-025)' rendering the usage ladder and allocation period (a module-01 concern). Likewise L75761 gives MOD-DOH-13 the purpose 'Read-only tenant view of tier, usage, suspension status AND Platform Access History' and L98159 gives it 'Read-only rendering of tier, usage and suspension status'. Do not let the usage ladder land in module 13.

PLATFORM ACCESS HISTORY IS CLAIMED BY BOTH MOD-DOH-13 (SLICE 4) AND MOD-DOH-11 (SLICE 10). The screen is module 13's at L14852, L26073, L48116 and L107861, but the Platform Access History control rows at L58075 and L97134 and the End-session rows at L87560 and L97084 are all tagged MOD-DOH-11 Audit and Retention. Since the gates at L46193 and L110975 require the history to READ THE SAME AUDIT RECORDS rather than a separate view, slice 4 cannot ship a working Platform Access History without the slice-10 audit store, or must ship a read-through view whose backing store lands later. This is a hard cross-slice dependency and it is not declared anywhere in the extract.

THE END-SESSION ROLE LIST HAS FOUR MUTUALLY INCONSISTENT ANSWERS. Tenant Admin only (L1476, L4599, L10902, L51712, L58038, L117497); Tenant Admin + platform Support (L21449); Tenant Admin + any tenant user seeing the banner (L23599, L45700, L103272, L107821); Tenant Admin + Supervisor + Quality Manager + Read-only Auditor (L29168, the module card). The role rule at L29199 says the widest reading is deliberate: 'the control belongs to the tenant; deliberately available to any signed-in tenant web user rather than only to the Tenant Admin'. Build the widest set and treat the narrow rows as drafting drift — but get it confirmed, because L21449 granting the control to the platform-side Support role contradicts the whole premise of a tenant-held control.

DOES THE END-SESSION CONTROL EXIST ON THE COMPLIANCE-EMERGENCY BANNER? L51712 says the control ends 'an in-session support OR compliance-emergency access session'. L64810 says flatly that no End-session control is offered for the compliance-emergency class 'because an emergency access the tenant could terminate would not be an emergency access'. L14878 records the same gap as a contradiction with governing decision DEC-EMEREND-001, noting 8.15.1 attaches the banner and control explicitly to the normal support session and says nothing about the other two classes. Unresolved. The safe build is banner-on-all-three, End-session-on-support-only, with the emergency class carrying the automatic post-session report instead.

DEC-SUSP-001 IS THE DEFINING UNRESOLVED CONTRADICTION FOR MOD-DOH-01 AND IT IS EVERYWHERE. Soft-suspension release is 'explicit operator signal, not a payment event' at 4.2.4 and 'Automatic on payment' at 8.9.2 / Part IX, on a platform that 4.2.1 and 8.12 say has no payment integration. 20 extracted instances, first at L2201, recurring at L3914, L7739, L13272, L21304, L26967, L41353, L44927, L50067, L54956, L58675, L64903, L71159, L78344, L81024, L94810, L96507, L101033, L111180, L113743. source-reconciliation records an ADOPTED working position dated 2026-08-14: operator signal in the Super Admin console, payment path left open and unbuilt, both readings preserved. Confirmed by hard gate AC-51-33 (L114056). Build the operator signal; do not build a payment listener.

THE FIXED COMPLIANCE-SUSPENSION WORKER MESSAGE EXISTS IN TWO WORDINGS AND BOTH ARE CALLED VERBATIM-FIXED. 'Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved.' (4.2.3 / 7.11, at L19690, L50064, L51560, L81024, L110776, L117373) versus 'Operation suspended — your work has been saved.' (8.9.2, at L44923, L71171, L100694, L114674). The shorter form drops the only actionable instruction. Governing decisions recorded inconsistently as DEC-MSG-001 (L5263, L44923, L71171) and DEC-SUSPMSG-001 (L114674), with L100694 noting 'proposed identifier not yet assigned'. Gate AC-CMD-007 (L12692) forbids rewording. Pick the Part IV form and record the decision id.

THE SUPPORT BANNER STRING ALSO HAS TWO WORDINGS. L5263 records 'viewing your tenant' at 4.12.2 versus 'viewing your workspace' at 8.15.1, alongside the compliance-message divergence. The hard gate at L23801 fixes the workspace form. Both are load-bearing UI copy under a no-reword gate.

WHAT HAPPENS AFTER A TENANT ENDS A SESSION IS UNSPECIFIED. L61211 (DEC-SUPPORT-001): 4.12.2 and 8.15 give the End-session control but neither states a cool-down, a re-open limit, or notification of a re-open, so the control may be advisory in practice. L58302 (DEC-SUPEXCL-001): a standing per-engineer tenant exclusion list is not specified, so the tenant's objection depends on repeated manual termination. FB-SUPPORT-001 at L64730 records the terminal safe state for this as 'Not resolved here'. Slice 4 must decide re-open behaviour or ship a control the tenant can press forever.

'IMPERSONATION CONTROL' IS NAMED IN MOD-DOH-13'S SOURCE SECTION BUT NO IMPERSONATION FEATURE EXISTS. L17647 and L20175 (DEC-IMPERSONATE-001): 4.12.3 lists 'cross-tenant visibility and impersonation control' among the functions, while Part VIII defines no impersonation feature, closes the access classes at three, makes support read-only without exception, and AC-16-12 (L20225) forbids any acting-as-role control or banner on any surface. The module's own scope gate at L29172 lists 'impersonation control' among the things NOT reachable from the Hub. Read it as a guardrail, not a feature — but the decision is open.

MOD-DOH-13 OWNS NO BUSINESS OBJECT AT ALL, AND THAT IS A FINDING NOT AN OMISSION. Zero object rows fall in the module card's line range (L29160-L29320), and every object it renders — support session, compliance-emergency session, JBS grant, platform announcement, post-session report — is authoritative on SURF-SA. Its only write is the tenant-initiated session termination, which writes to a SURF-SA-owned object and mirrors to the tenant audit log. Model it as a read/mirror module plus one command, with no local schema.

MOD-DOH-01 OWNS EXACTLY ONE OBJECT. OBJ-DOH-TENSTATE 'Tenant state' at L26874 (authoritative_owner_surface SURF-DOH, administering surface the Super Admin console) and its history table tenant_state_history (OBJ-005 at L7711, OBJ-DOH-TENSTATE register row at L26157). Everything else the module shows — Tenant, Tier record, Usage Ledger Entry, ladder state, Pilot, Tenant Group — is SURF-SA-owned. The split ownership on the single object it does own (Hub is authoritative, console administers) needs an explicit read/write contract before build.

THE MODULE'S ROLE LIST CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON WHETHER SUPERVISORS SEE THE TIER VIEW. L26890 states Supervisor may_not 'View own tier/entitlements/caps/consumption (Unavailable)', yet the same module card at L26866 lists Supervisor, Quality Manager, Read-only Auditor and Worker among roles_allowed, and L22019/L29178 list four roles for module 13. Read 'roles_allowed' as 'roles the module touches', not 'roles that can see the screen', and drive screen visibility from the L26885/L26888/L26890 role rules.

MOD-DOH-01'S 'ONBOARDING ROLE-MAPPING WORKSHEET' ROW IS NOT FROZEN SCOPE. The module row at L18024 carries id MOD-DOH-01 and screen SCR-DOH-ONBOARD-MAP with three live validation checks, roles Tenant Admin plus 'Implementation team member', but its classification is 'Recommendation - Research and Development' while every other MOD-DOH-01 row is 'SoW Fact'. Job-title-to-role mapping is also MOD-DOH-09 subject matter. Do not build it into slice 4 as module-01 scope without a client decision.

THE MODULE CARD'S OWN CROSS-REFERENCE POINTS AT A MODULE THAT MAY NOT EXIST AS DESCRIBED. OBJ-DOH-TENSTATE's key_relationships at L26874 name 'MOD-DOH-12 tenant read view' and 'MOD-DOH-18 data set 5', while the tenant read view of tier and usage is module 01's own SCR-DOH-002/SCR-DOH-03 and MOD-DOH-12 is Integration settings (SCR-DOH-022 at L26072, SCR-DOH-21 at L48115). L29052 confirms WF-DOH-12-INT terminates in a 'read-only tier and usage view rendered'. Settle whether the tier/usage read view is rendered by module 01 or module 12 before either team builds it. MOD-DOH-18 is slice 6.

NO FALLBACK CONTRACT WAS EXTRACTED INSIDE EITHER MODULE CARD. Zero failures_fallbacks rows fall in L26860-L27080 or L29160-L29320. The relevant contracts live under other prefixes and must be pulled in by hand: for module 01, FB-SUSP-001 through FB-SUSP-008 (L64953, L65066, L65068, L65190, L65192, L65277, L65319, L65323) and FB-TIER-001/002/003 (L11931, L12044, L12157); for module 13, FB-SUPPORT-001/002/003 (L64730, L64726, L64728). FB-SUSP-002's terminal safe state is explicitly the DEC-SUSP-001 stalemate: 'a tenant that remains in soft suspension, operating normally, until a human clears it'.

THE ANNOUNCEMENTS FEATURE IS THE THINNEST-SPECIFIED PART OF EITHER MODULE. Only one control row exists (L115575 'Platform announcement banner', module_id MOD-DOH-13) and it records NO allowed_roles and no acknowledge or dismiss behaviour; the tenant-side state vocabulary is two states, active and expired (L29187), against six on the SURF-SA object (L9306). modules.purpose: Module identity card (L28505): "Configure who exists in the tenant, what each may do, and where; enforce it across all five surfaces from one place." The blueprint restates the purpose twelve more times with differing emphasis and the wordings are not identical: "Band A module for tenant permissions, roles and access" (L2436); "Tenant-side permissions matrix for the five fixed roles" (L11141); "Administers the tenant role domain; renders the by-person and by-capability permission views and the refusal-explanation view" (L14262); "Where user accounts, roles and access scopes are configured" (L17475); "Five fixed roles, three scopes, two-track login, multi-role, mandatory-role enforcement" (L22015, L25965, L47249); "Role assignment and the three scope dimensions" (L52740); "Role assignment, scope assignment, revocation and offboarding" (L60782); "Tenant user creation, role assignment and three-dimensional scope assignment" (L75820); "Authority evaluated at the attempted action, never on a sweep" (L98155); "Five fixed roles, three scopes, role-scope assignment store" (L116397). Classification is SoW Fact at §4.8-§4.8.4, §3.5, §4.11.1, §4.13.3; the identity card, the permission-matrix statuses, the fail-closed rule and the storyboard are Derived Clarification (L28666 source-status paragraph). Owning surface SURF-DOH (L28507). Dependencies: MOD-DOH-02 for scope values, MOD-DOH-01 for the tenant suspension class, MOD-DOH-12 for single sign-on (L28513). Fallbacks FB-DOH-WRITE-002 for configuration writes, FB-DOH-CORE-001 for reads, plus the authentication ladder of §19.1.1 (L28516).
