hardGates.id: unnumbered (module card, Business purpose and rules)
hardGates.statement: There are five fixed roles at V1; custom roles are deferred beyond V1. There is no 'Quality Director' role, and Job Owner is a field, not a role.
Multi-role users are allowed with additive permissions; the audit log records the user identity and the action — never an 'acting as role' fiction.
Two mandatory-role rules are enforced: at least one Tenant Admin always exists, and an approver role must exist whenever a Job exists. Delegation is deferred beyond V1.

The permission system fails closed: an unresolvable permission denies the request. Enforcement point: permission resolution fallback. NOTE: this is the ONLY one of the module card's nine acceptance criteria (AC-DOH-09-1..9, L28615-L28623) the extract flags is_hard_gate true — the other eight are equally absolute in the prose.
A permission applies only within the scope of the grant that conferred it; scopes do not merge across grants.
Platform-fixed prohibitions refuse the action regardless of held roles, grants, scopes, tier, or account, including the root.
While DEC-XROLE-001 is open, assigning a tenant role to an identity that holds a platform console role is refused, and the refusal names the open decision.
No surface renders a role selector, an 'acting as' control, an 'acting as' banner, or any session-level role context.
No impersonation mechanism exists on any surface while DEC-IMPERSONATE-001 is open.
Removing the last Tenant Admin is refused, with the rule named, and no override exists on any surface — including within support sessions.
Creating the first Job in a tenant with no approver-capable role holder is refused with the same rule named.
Cached device permissions are honoured only within the offline credential-trust window and are then graded down per section 15.4.
Every cell of every matrix carries exactly one status token from the closed set; a blank, ellipsis, dash, or 'same as above' is a defect that fails acceptance.
The runtime policy decision point and the rendered Roles pane are generated from one configuration source.
No tenant role type can obtain any authenticated session against the Super Admin platform console under any configuration, including multi-role assignment. Restated as AC-RBAC-401 at L21943.
Every denial writes an audit event carrying identity, attempted action, object, object state, and the failing test.
Disabling or hiding a control never changes the authorisation outcome of the equivalent application programming interface call.
Every mutating route across all five surfaces is registered with the policy decision point; route-inventory coverage is 100 percent at release.
A single sign-on assertion carrying a role claim not assigned in the Delivery Operations Hub grants nothing.
Queued captures uploaded after a permission revocation are preserved and quarantined, never accepted as official records and never discarded.
Every module of all four tenant-facing surfaces carries a status for all five tenant role types, with no blank cells (62 tenant modules).
Every Client Decision Required cell denies at runtime and names its decision identifier in the denial.
Forward parity: every rendered control for every identity shape corresponds to a permitted action. Failing count must be zero.
Reverse parity: every permitted action corresponds to a rendered control or to a capability explicitly recorded as headless. Failing count must be zero.
Floor parity: no identity shape, tenant configuration, suspension state, or caller class permits an action that would breach a platform floor or one of the six enforced invariants.

The login is the credential, not the device: identity, qualifications, language preference and attribution travel with the worker onto any conformant device, and a shared tablet confers nothing by itself. Restated at L75998.
Removal of the last approver-capable role while Jobs exist is refused.
No mutating operation succeeds for the Read-only Auditor on any surface, through any interface; any mutating request is refused and recorded as a security-relevant event.
Attribution is always by individual identity, never by device; every worker has their own platform identity and login and the credential is the person's, never the device's.

No tenant role can: override a specification gate or the evaluation gate from any surface (L17281); pause or stop a run from the Command Center (L17282); edit any record or configuration from the Command Center (L17283); create Jobs or runs from the Command Center (L17284); make any configuration looser than the platform floor (L17285); alter or delete evidence or audit history (L17286); reach another tenant or the Super Admin platform console (L17287).

A scope narrows a role and never widens it; the three scope dimensions are held simultaneously and are orthogonal. A grant is additive and time-bounded and may never create authority a role does not already contain.
The platform stores no object of kind persona; a job title may be recorded only as free-text reference metadata and is excluded from every authorization decision.
Every effective permission resolves to at least one of: a role type, a scope, a grant, a qualification, or a temporary grant. No other source of authority exists.
Every audit entry names the acting identity. No audit entry contains an acting-as-role field.
A name qualifies as a role only if it appears in the five-row tenant table or the four-row console table; nothing else is a role.
The platform exposes no create-role, edit-role, or clone-role control on any surface at V1; the roles endpoint returns exactly nine role types.
Deny-by-default: an unresolved or unreachable permission condition produces a refusal, never a grant. An absolute rule that cannot be evaluated is treated as violated.
Deny by default; never fail open; never authorise from a cached decision whose configuration version is older than the last committed permission change for that identity.
The last Tenant Admin cannot be removed; the last approver-capable user cannot be removed while a Job exists.
No custom role can be created at V1, and no Quality Director role exists.
Scope values may never cross tenants; cross-tenant data isolation is platform-fixed.
Removing the last Tenant Admin is refused, naming the rule.
Removing the last approver-capable role while any Job exists is refused, naming the rule.
A role correction is recorded as a removal event and an addition event, never as an in-place edit.

No surface shows a revocation as in force on a device before that device has acknowledged the command; a revocation is recorded immediately and in force on a device at that device's next sync or at expiry of the offline trust window.
The Read-only Auditor cannot reach any Client Command Center route.
An expired, revoked or superseded invitation cannot activate an account.
A failed or abandoned identity proof leaves no partially activated account and no usable credential material.
Requesting an invitation status without an authenticated console session returns no information about whether the account exists.
An invitation is single-use: a second use of the same link after activation is refused.
Authentication is not authorization. Role assignment stays inside the platform; an assertion carrying a group or role claim is untrusted input, logged and ignored.
Platform and tenant roles are separate security domains; a Tenant Admin has no platform authority; a tenant-federated identity provider can never yield a platform console session.

The platform maps the asserted subject to exactly one existing platform user record within exactly one tenant; where no such record exists, sign-in is refused, because there is no just-in-time provisioning at the first version. Carries open decision DEC-SSO-001 (L95907).
Every permission-matrix cell in the blueprint carries an explicit status from the closed set; no cell is blank. A blank cell is a build-blocking defect.
The platform presents exactly five surfaces and no sixth — enforcement point is surface enumeration per role, which this module computes.

The integration surface is closed at the first version. Adding an integration is a scope decision taken by the client, never an engineering convenience. Enforcement: release planning and the deny-by-default egress allow-list.
No integration may weaken a platform floor. Tenants may make the platform stricter than default and may never make it looser; the platform rejects a looser-than-floor value rather than logging it.
No integration participates in the deviation-triggering path. No external system and no AI service may sit between a measurement and its severity classification.

Every value not present in the Statement of Work is marked TBD — Client Decision Required with an owner; inventing one would create a false contractual commitment. Applies to timeouts, retries, rate limits, RTO/RPO and cadences on every integration card.
Authentication is not authorization. Role assignment stays inside the platform; an assertion carrying a group or role claim is untrusted input, logged and ignored. (Shared gate with MOD-DOH-09.)

Platform and tenant roles are separate security domains; a Tenant Admin has no platform authority; a tenant-federated identity provider can never yield a platform console session. (Shared gate with MOD-DOH-09.)

The platform maps the asserted subject to exactly one existing platform user record within exactly one tenant; where no such record exists, sign-in is refused — there is no just-in-time provisioning at V1. Open decision DEC-SSO-001 (L95907) asks whether this should change; adopted interim is option (a), refuse.
In-app notifications cannot be muted and are one of exactly two notification channels; the only channels anywhere in the platform are in-app and email.
A notification is never the only mechanism enforcing safety, a hold, qualification, authorization, approval, suspension, or a device command. Email is the escalation's carrier, never its enforcement.
Sending is not delivery, delivery is not opening, opening is not acknowledgement, and acknowledgement is not the business action. No surface may collapse these states.

External notification recipients and quiet hours are outside the first version. A tenant cannot direct AVIIXA email to a distribution list outside its own user records except the named tenant contact address.
A tenant's manufacturing memory is isolated to that tenant: nothing is shared with another tenant, and nothing is used as external training data.
A tenant at its per-tenant token ceiling produces an explicit unavailability, not a silently truncated answer.
Model output is treated as untrusted input, validated, never executed as commands; guards against prompt injection.
The stub is honest and stays honest: a stubbed inbound endpoint returning 501 must not be quietly upgraded to accept payloads in a patch release.
Reserved external fields are held NULL and mean nothing until activation; they must not be repurposed for any other use in the interim.
The run_source enumeration is complete at four values: manual, auto_scheduled, erp_inbound and api_inbound. At the first version only manual is producible.
An inbound system is a creator; it is never an approver. The Job state machine and the creator-cannot-approve rule bind it exactly as they bind a human.
There is no invoicing, no payment execution, and no pricing engine anywhere on the platform.
The usage export carries counts and metadata only, never operational content: no worker name, measurement value, evidence photograph or workflow content.

The usage ladder produces flags, never enforcement: 80 per cent banner, 100 per cent escalation, 100-125 per cent burst tolerance with burst entry recorded, above 125 per cent a flag opening a commercial conversation.
An item on the exclusion list is answered by citing it, never by re-arguing it; changing an entry is a client scope decision.

No integration failure may reach the deterministic layer. An integration outage is strictly less powerful than an emergency pause, so it cannot do what an emergency pause cannot do. No integration failure may make an offline device appear remotely controlled or make a command appear applied.
An incident is not closed when the dependency returns; it is closed when the records agree.

Three incompatible SCR-DOH numbering schemes (SCR-DOH-NNN zero-padded, SCR-DOH-NN unpadded, SCR-DOH-MNEMONIC) coexist and nothing reconciles them.

ONE SCREEN IDENTIFIER, TWO SCREENS. SCR-DOH-PERM-ROLES is 'role reference pane' at L17609 and 'The mandatory-role guard (SB-16-05)' at L20641. Separately, the Hub refusal view exists twice under different identifiers: SCR-DOH-ROLE-04 'Why was I refused' (L14267) and SCR-DOH-DENY-01 'Delivery Operations Hub refusal' (L14573), both reached by the same control at L14573.

THE USER-ACCOUNT STATE VOCABULARY IS STATED FOUR IRRECONCILABLE WAYS AND THE ROLE-GRANT VOCABULARY THREE. User: provisioned/active/disabled (L8350); the ten-state lifecycle Requested..EvidenceRetained (L18939); active/suspended_by_tenant_state/archived (L28512, the module card); Requested/Validating/Created/Active/Dormant/Refused (L67543). Role grant: granted/revoked (L8380); the nine-state Proposed..Historical (L19077); assigned/removed (L28512). Slice 4 cannot ship without picking one, and the source picks none.

THE PERMISSION-MATRIX STATUS SET IS PUBLISHED AS SIX TOKENS AT L1200 AND AS NINE TOKENS AT L10238, L14234 AND L20811. Two hard gates make blank or wrong cells build-blocking (AC-DOC-006 L856, AC-RBAC-001 L20781) and AC-RBAC-411 (L22101) requires a status for all five roles on all 62 tenant modules. The token set must be fixed before any MOD-DOH-09 matrix is generated. The six-token set also omits 'Cached read-only while offline' and 'Queued while offline', which MOD-DOH-09 needs for the offline trust window.

DEC-ROLE-001 AND DEC-PLUS-001 ARE BOTH OPEN AND BOTH ARE NAMED AS MOD-DOH-09'S OPEN DECISIONS AT L60782. DEC-PLUS-001 is recorded as structurally unresolvable from the source; the standing instruction is that every 'Supervisor+' / 'QM+' cell must be implemented as an enumerated grant list, never a rank comparison, and that 'Supervisor and above' excludes Tenant Admin. DEC-ROLE-001 (Plant Manager / Quality Director) must never silently create a sixth role; the roles endpoint returns exactly nine role types (L17662).

DEC-AUDEXPORT-001 DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS A CONTROL THIS SLICE SHIPS. The 'Save as document' control at L14355 lists the Read-only Auditor in allowed_roles, while L16893 states export is rendered as Client Decision Required in every matrix cell for that role and 'no fragment assumes it exists'. AC-RBAC-602 (L23110) requires Client Decision Required cells to deny at runtime naming the decision identifier. Build the deny path, not the export path, until the client rules.

DEC-SSO-001 (L95907) IS THE ONLY OPEN DECISION SPECIFIC TO MOD-DOH-12'S SSO FEATURE, AND THE MODULE'S OWN COVERAGE-MAP CELL SAYS THERE IS NONE. L60785 reads 'Not applicable — enterprise resource planning integration is deferred to V2 by the source' in the open-decisions column, which is not true of the SSO half of the module. Adopted interim: refuse sign-in for unknown subjects; no just-in-time provisioning (L95794).

DEC-XROLE-001 AND DEC-IMPERSONATE-001 GATE MOD-DOH-09 WHILE STILL OPEN. AC-16-07 (L20135) refuses assigning a tenant role to an identity holding a console role, naming the decision. AC-16-17 (L20230) requires that no impersonation mechanism exists on any surface. Both are interim postures with no adopted resolution (L20074, L20175). Build the refusals; do not build the mechanisms.

DEC-DELEG-001 (L17920) SITS ON A CONTROL THIS SLICE SHIPS. The Grants panel control at L17502 manages the authoring grant and the Agent Author capability, while §4.8.4 defers delegation beyond V1 (module-card matrix row L28528) and §5.18/§5.15.4 describe an 'Agent Author delegation'. Also unresolved: GRANT-STU-AUTHOR is owned by SURF-DOH at L76411 and by SURF-STU at L16457, and is administered from MOD-STU-18 at L34631 as well as from this module's screen.

THREE INTEGRATION-IDENTIFIER NAMESPACES DESCRIBE THE SAME THING. Chapter 27.8 publishes five cards (INT-SSO-001 L51788, INT-CRED-001 L51836, INT-MAIL-001 L51860, INT-AI-001 L51884, INT-ERP-001 L51908). Chapter 45.2 publishes seven (adds INT-EMB-001 and INT-USAGE-001, rows at L95634-L95640) with TEST-45-002-01 at L95760 asserting exactly seven. MOD-DOH-12's key functions at L25968 use a third scheme: INT-DOH-SSO, INT-DOH-EMAIL, INT-DOH-AICOMPUTE, INT-DOH-ERPSTUB. The module card's own Objects-affected field names only INT-DOH-SSO (L29031).

MOD-DOH-12 CLAIMS FEATURES WHOSE OWNING SURFACE IS THE SUPER ADMIN CONSOLE. Of the seven Chapter-45 integrations, only INT-SSO-001, INT-CRED-001, INT-MAIL-001 and INT-ERP-001 name the Delivery Operations Hub as owning surface (L95634, L95635, L95636, L95639). INT-AI-001 (L95637), INT-EMB-001 (L95638) and INT-USAGE-001 (L95640) name the Super Admin platform console. Yet FEAT-DOH-12-2.2 claims bundled compute (L29089) and FEAT-DOH-12-3.2 claims the tier and usage view (L29093). Slice 4 must be told what it BUILDS versus what it only RENDERS read-only.

THE TENANT CONTACT EMAIL FIELD IS TAGGED TO TWO MODULES IN DIFFERENT SLICES. It is a MOD-DOH-12 permission-matrix row at L29043 and a MOD-DOH-12 storyboard card at L29121, but the rendered control at L96010 is tagged MOD-DOH-10, which the build order places in slice 10. Same problem for 'Configure single sign-on', which is a MOD-DOH-09 matrix row at L28530 and a MOD-DOH-12 matrix row at L29042.

THE EXTRACT AND THE PROSE DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT IS A HARD GATE. On the MOD-DOH-09 card, only AC-DOH-09-9 (L28623) is flagged is_hard_gate true; AC-DOH-09-1..8 (L28615-L28622) are equally absolute in wording. On the MOD-DOH-12 card, only two rules are flagged (L29009, L29015); the email-vendor, bundled-compute and read-only-usage rules are not, though Chapter 45 states them absolutely (L95945, L95957, L96109, L96505). Do not treat the is_hard_gate flag as the gate inventory.

MOD-DOH-09'S roles_allowed IS STATED FOUR DIFFERENT WAYS ACROSS ITS THIRTEEN MODULE RECORDS. Tenant Admin only at L2436, L11141, L14262, L17475, L25965, L47249, L52740, L60782, L75820 and L98155; Tenant Admin plus Read-only Auditor at L22015; all five tenant roles at L28503; empty at L116397. Only the card's own permission matrix (L28520-L28533) resolves it, and it is the artefact to build from.

TWO MODULE-09-SHAPED WORKFLOW IDENTIFIERS HAVE NO CARD, NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA AND NO TESTS. WF-DOH-CREATE-USER and WF-DOH-ASSIGN-ROLE both appear only in the Tenant Admin inventory table at L16503. WF-WKR-004 (L52892) and WF-WKR-005 (L52924) have full cards with AC-* and TEST-* sets. The two are probably duplicates of WF-WKR-004 but the source never says so; if they are distinct, slice 4 is missing two workflow contracts.

THE OFFLINE CREDENTIAL-TRUST WINDOW IS A MOD-DOH-09 SETTING WITH A NON-SLICE-4 ENFORCEMENT POINT. Default approximately 24 hours with a platform ceiling of 72 hours (L28568, AC-DOH-09-6 at L28620), but the gates that enforce it are on the Frontline device (AC-16-42 L20661, AC-GOAL-045 L2117) and the terminal behaviour is graded down per §15.4. Slice 4 owns the setting and its 72-hour ceiling validation; it does not own the enforcement.

THE NINE ACCESS CONDITIONS ARE PUBLISHED IN TWO DIFFERENT ORDERS. Definition order at L14514 begins with Role permission; evaluation order at L14531 begins with Safety controls. The 'Why was I refused' view (SCR-DOH-ROLE-04 L14267, control at L14573) shows which of the nine failed, so it must render the evaluation order or it will mislead. The source does not say which order the view uses.

NO SCREEN, CONTROL OR OBJECT IN EITHER MODULE CARRIES A STATED LINE-LEVEL OWNER FOR THE SIGN-IN SURFACE ROLES. The five sign-in controls at L95829 and L95832 (Work email address, Continue, Sign in with a platform credential, Platform credential, Sign in) all carry an empty allowed_roles list. SCR-DOH-01 at L48095 says 'All five tenant roles'. Slice 4 should treat L48095 as the answer and record the gap.

IDENTIFIER-INDEX COVERAGE IS PARTIAL AND MUST NOT BE USED AS A LOCATOR OF RECORD. registries/raw/identifier-index.json returns only three lines for MOD-DOH-09 (3799, 3901, 11141) and three for MOD-DOH-12 (3904, 4797, 4805), while a direct grep of the frozen source finds 39 occurrences of MOD-DOH-09 and 18 of MOD-DOH-12. Every locator in this map came from the extract chunks or a direct grep, not from the index.

value.topic: SURF-DOH slice 4 cross-cutting spine — tenant lifecycle, tier model tenant-side face, five-role permission surface, and the MOD-DOH-13 platform-administration window (MOD-DOH-01, MOD-DOH-13, with MOD-DOH-12/17 tenant read faces)

findings.claim: MOD-DOH-01 (Tenant Lifecycle and Tier Operations) is the module that owns this spine. Its stated job is threefold and nothing more: enforce the tenant's current state across every screen and API, record every transition, and give the tenant a read-only view of its own tier, usage and suspension status. Administration of the lifecycle (onboarding, tier assignment, suspension, reactivation, archival) belongs to the Super Admin platform console, not the Hub.

AUTHORITATIVE STATE SET (Hub view): tenant operating states are active, soft_suspended, hard_suspended, compliance_suspended, archived — five, declared on the MOD-DOH-01 identity card 'States' row. Two further vocabularies sit on the same row: tier-change states none / pending_downgrade (2), and usage-ladder states below_80 / at_or_above_80 / at_or_above_100_burst / above_125_flagged (4).

LEGAL TRANSITIONS, as drawn by MOD-DOH-01's own state diagram: Active→SoftSuspended (non-payment 30d default); Soft→Active (client team clears the commercial hold); Soft→HardSuspended (non-payment 60d or commercial action); Hard→Active (lifted by client platform team after resolution); Active|Soft|Hard→ComplianceSuspended (security or terms-of-service cause — enterable from ANY state, because its cause is not commercial); Compliance→Active (decision of the client platform team following review); Active→Archived; Archived→Active (reactivation inside the archival windows). Every arrow is recorded in tenant_state_history and the audit log.

WHO CAUSES EACH TRANSITION: every transition without exception is caused by the client's platform team from the Super Admin platform console. No tenant role can change a suspension state or a tier ceiling — 'Change a suspension state' is Explicitly prohibited for all five tenant roles, and tenant state is read-only to every tenant role. The single tenant-initiated act in the whole module is the self-service tier upgrade (and the downgrade REQUEST, which records a request only).

SOFT SUSPENSION — blocked write classes, stated 'exactly': creation of new Jobs, new Workers, new locations, new shifts, new parts, and ALL configuration edits including tenant settings, roles and permissions, and notification policy. Open 'exactly': the full operational pipeline — supervisors create and schedule runs, assign and substitute workers; execution and capture continue; Summaries compute; QM review proceeds; clearances operate; notifications and audit run; and qualification RECERTIFICATION on existing workers stays open, explicitly because it operates the existing account rather than growing it.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-04 (workers/qualifications), MOD-DOH-02, MOD-DOH-03, MOD-DOH-09, MOD-DOH-19 — all slice 4

findings.claim: HARD SUSPENSION — blocked: everything except the enumerated completion pipeline; no new runs can be created. Open 'exactly': the completion pipeline only — in-flight runs complete with step execution, data capture and sync continuing; substitution remains available WHERE NEEDED to complete an in-flight run; the Summaries of those runs compute and close through the standard lifecycle; mandatory notifications and the audit log continue. Everything else is read-only.

COMPLIANCE SUSPENSION — blocked: all logins blocked immediately; in-flight runs stopped. Open: nothing. Devices receive the stop over the command channel at next sync. Exit is only by decision of the client's platform team following review. Entry into a compliance-suspended tenant is possible only through the dual-authorised compliance-emergency path, the only platform access class with write capability into tenant data.

WHAT A SUSPENDED TENANT CAN STILL DO — soft state, enumerated on SCR-DOH-SUSPEND-SOFT: Open Platform Access History; Contact platform support; continue using every unaffected screen. Explicitly disabled with named messages: Create a Job, Edit a tenant setting, Enrol a device, and Dismiss the banner (that control does not exist while the state persists).

WHAT A SUSPENDED TENANT CAN STILL DO — hard state, enumerated on SCR-DOH-SUSPEND-HARD: Open the review queue; Open Platform Access History; Contact platform support. Disabled: create a run, create any master data, edit any setting, publish in the Studio. Screen title is 'workspace, account read-only'; status line carries the count of in-flight runs remaining.

WHAT A SUSPENDED TENANT CAN STILL DO — compliance state: nothing on any web surface (all logins blocked, so the Hub, Command Center and Studio are unreachable for every role). On the device the locked screen has enabled actions 'None. The message is the entire interface'; continuing the run, signing in as a different worker, exporting or viewing local data, and dismissing the message are all controls that DO NOT EXIST rather than being disabled.

SUSPENSION MESSAGING BY AUDIENCE, stated 'exactly' as a closed 3x2 table. Soft or Hard: Tenant Admin sees a banner in the Hub and NO OTHER USER SEES ANYTHING; non-admin web users see nothing; workers on mobile see nothing. Compliance: Tenant Admin and non-admin web users both see 'Suspended pending review — contact platform support.'; workers on mobile see the fixed message 'Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved.' — quoted verbatim and fixed platform-wide.

THE FIVE-ROLE PERMISSION SURFACE for MOD-DOH-01 is a 12-row matrix with an explicit status in every one of the 60 cells. Rows: view own tier/entitlements/caps/consumption; view ladder position and burst-band status; view suspension status; see the suspension banner in soft or hard state; see the compliance-suspension message; request a tier upgrade; request a tier downgrade; execute a downgrade; change a suspension state; change ladder thresholds; view tenant-group membership; read tenant_state_history through the audit log.
findings.bindingOn: Tenant Admin, Supervisor, Quality Manager, Read-only Auditor, Worker

findings.claim: PER-ROLE READING OF THAT MATRIX. Tenant Admin: Read-only on tier/ladder/suspension/tenant_state_history; Allowed to see the soft-or-hard banner; Allowed to request an upgrade (self-service, effective immediately) and a downgrade (request only). Read-only Auditor: identical READ rights to the Tenant Admin (tier, ladder, suspension, tenant_state_history) but Explicitly prohibited on every action. Supervisor and Quality Manager: Unavailable on every view row, Explicitly prohibited on every action row; both see nothing at all in soft or hard state. Worker: Unavailable/prohibited on everything; sees nothing on mobile in soft or hard. All five roles see the compliance message.

WHAT IS IRREVERSIBLE. Exactly one act is named irreversible platform-wide: anonymisation of worker personal data at 24 months after archival for standard commercial tenants — the identity link is severed, a named worker becomes an opaque worker number, and every measurement, result and piece of evidence survives. Switching a tenant into Regulated-Industry mode later does not, and cannot, restore already-anonymised identities. Regulated-Industry tenants never anonymise. Reversing anonymisation is 'Not applicable — the act is irreversible by construction'.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-17, MOD-DOH-11 (slice 10) — but the warning obligation surfaces in slice 4 tenant screens

findings.claim: WHAT IS NOT IRREVERSIBLE, and must not be built as if it were: nothing is purged anywhere on the platform. Archival is not deletion — archived operational, configuration and audit data stays inside the tenant's hot-retrievability horizon (default 15 years, set per tenant in the Super Admin console) and then tiers to lower-cost storage, still retrievable. Retention is uniform across tiers and is not at any point a tier-gated feature. Reactivation from archived back to active is a real transition inside the windows.

REACTIVATION AND ARCHIVAL, stated 'exactly' as a six-row table: Soft lifts immediately when the client's team clears the commercial hold; Hard is lifted by the client's platform team after resolution; Compliance is lifted only by decision of the client's platform team following review; archival 0-6 months reactivates at no fee; 6-12 months for an engineering-time fee; after 12 months a FRESH TENANT ONLY, with historical data remaining exportable for a retrieval fee.
findings.bindingOn: FUNC-DOH-01-3.1.1; the client's platform team only, all tenant roles prohibited

findings.claim: THE TIER MODEL, tenant-side face. Three tiers by monthly Worker-Shift allocation: Starter fewer than 100, Growth 100 to 199, Enterprise 200 and above. Tier records carry entitlements, limits and thresholds and NEVER price metadata. There is no payment integration, no invoicing and no pricing engine at any tier — pricing and invoicing sit entirely outside the platform in the client's own commercial systems.

NO HUB CAPABILITY IS TIER-LOCKED AT V1. Custom Job Types, Service Type tags, single sign-on and retention are available uniformly across all tiers. Tiers differ ONLY in allocation ceilings and thresholds. Active Locations are metered at Site level only. The per-tenant feature-enablement machinery exists in the Super Admin console for future differentiation but is not exercised against the Hub at V1.
findings.bindingOn: every SURF-DOH module — do not build a tier gate into any Hub screen

findings.claim: THE ONE V1 TIER GATE IS OUTSIDE THE HUB. The Agent Author capability is tier-gated to Growth and Enterprise and Unavailable on Starter. This is a SURF-STU (Studio) gate read from the tenant's tier record, so it does not contradict the no-Hub-tier-locking rule — but slice 4 must store the tier record in a shape that can answer a tier-entitlement question, because a non-Hub surface already asks one.

THE WORKER-SHIFT METER, the consumption metric the tenant screen renders: one worker attached to work within one calendar shift counts once regardless of how many runs they touch; where a substitution occurs, each worker who actually worked counts one. The allocation period is monthly. The definition is written into the tier record itself so the meter is contractually visible per tenant, and it is quoted verbatim on the tenant screen.

THE WORKER-SHIFT COUNT IS SYSTEM-ONLY. FUNC-DOH-01-1.1.1 states 'Roles allowed: none — this is a system function with no human actor' and 'Roles prohibited: all five tenant roles and all four platform roles may not create or edit a Worker-Shift count.' There is no manual meter adjustment anywhere for anyone.

HOW A TIER CHANGE REACHES A TENANT SCREEN — UPGRADE. Initiated self-service by the Tenant Admin (or by platform support through its own console), effective IMMEDIATELY. The tier record updates; consumption is NEVER reset and carries forward against the new ceiling (80 consumed of a 100 Starter ceiling stays 80 against a 199 Growth ceiling); the transition writes tenant_state_history and the audit log in the same transaction; the ladder recomputes against the new ceiling and the banner clears if the position falls below 80 percent.

HOW A TIER CHANGE REACHES A TENANT SCREEN — DOWNGRADE. Requested by the Tenant Admin, executed ONLY by the client's platform team from the Super Admin console. There is no mid-cycle change: the current period plays out at the current tier. A pending downgrade is tracked and labelled and is SUPERSEDED if another tier change is made first, with the superseded request recorded rather than deleted. Where the target ceiling is below current consumption the downgrade queues and a 'pending downgrade' status shows until it fits.

HOW A CAP REACHES A TENANT SCREEN — THE USAGE LADDER. Thresholds 80 / 100 / 125 percent are per-tenant defaults, set and tunable per tenant in the Super Admin console and Explicitly prohibited from tenant edit. Semantics: 80% = in-product banner; 100% = escalation notification; 100-125% = burst tolerance within which THE FLOOR KEEPS RUNNING, with a distinct burst-ENTRY event raised the moment consumption crosses into the band; above 125% the platform flags the tenant for the client's commercial conversation and the conversation happens outside the platform. No platform behaviour stops the floor at any threshold.

ALL LADDER AND STATE NOTIFICATIONS ARE MANDATORY BASELINE AND CANNOT BE SUPPRESSED BY ANY ROLE. Six notifications: 80% (NOTIF-DOH-01-1), 100% escalation re-notifying at 4h or 1h in Regulated-Industry mode (-2), burst-band entry (-3), above 125% (-4), ANY tenant state transition with email for suspension entries (-5), pending downgrade takes effect (-6). Subscription and tier lifecycle events always fire; in-app notifications cannot be muted.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-10 consumer; Tenant Admin as sole recipient

findings.claim: THE TENANT'S TIER SCREEN CARRIES FIVE REGIONS IN A FIXED ORDER and no control that changes a value: (1) the meter definition in plain words, quoted from the tier record; (2) current-period consumption against the ceiling as a number and a bar with a data-as-of timestamp; (3) the ladder position with the three thresholds marked and the burst band shaded; (4) the Active Locations count, metered at Site level only; (5) the suspension status. The only actions are the upgrade request and the downgrade request.

WHAT THE TENANT SEES OF PLATFORM ADMINISTRATION (MOD-DOH-13) is exactly three things: Platform Access History; the persistent support-session banner with its End-session control; and the platform announcement banner. The module's stated purpose is to make every platform-side access to the tenant's workspace visible to that tenant and give the tenant a control it can actually exercise. That screen is the only place a tenant observes the Super Admin console's existence, and there is no navigation from it into the console.

PLATFORM ACCESS HISTORY renders every platform-side access event against the tenant as a filtered view of the tenant's own audit log, with ALL THREE access classes mirrored identically: support sessions, the compliance-emergency procedure, and the granted delivery-partner (JBS) access class. SB-DOH-025 fixes the table columns: timestamp, access class, platform identity, reason, ticket reference and scope, filterable by class and date, with an export control, under the line 'This is a filtered view of your own audit log. Every platform-side access appears here.'

WHAT THE TENANT MUST NEVER SEE, enumerated at §4.12.4 and restated as AC-DOH-13-7: tier configuration and feature gates; cross-tenant visibility and impersonation control; pilot management; tenant-group management; the compliance emergency-access procedure itself; and all usage and billing administration. The closing sentence is 'The Hub shows the tenant its own position, read-only — nothing more.'

TENANT GROUPS ARE INVISIBLE TO THE TENANT, ABSOLUTELY. Multiple independent tenants per legal entity are supported, but at V1 the Tenant Group is an internal label of the client's team only, the platform performs NO operational behaviour on it, and it is not visible in any tenant's Hub. The MOD-DOH-01 matrix marks 'View tenant-group membership' as 'Not applicable' for all five roles with the reason stated in the cell, and AC-DOH-01-10 makes it testable: the tenant's Hub never displays a tenant-group label. Cross-tenant operational reporting is not in V1.
findings.bindingOn: all five tenant roles; MOD-DOH-01 and MOD-DOH-18

findings.claim: NO TENANT ROLE CAN REACH THE CONSOLE AT ALL. AC-RBAC-004: no tenant role type can obtain any authenticated session against the Super Admin platform console under any configuration, INCLUDING multi-role assignment. Platform and tenant roles are separate security domains; a Tenant Admin has no platform authority and there is no Tenant Super Admin.

PILOT TENANTS: invitation-only by the client, no public free trial. A pilot tenant is FUNCTIONALLY IDENTICAL to a paying tenant. Default pilot term 60 days, extendable to 90 at the client's discretion. Conversion preserves the tenant identifier — zero re-onboarding, no data migration. Pilots are excluded from the client's commercial aggregates. Pilot management is operated from the Super Admin console and FUNC-DOH-01-3.2.1 prohibits all tenant roles from conversion.

BRANDING: the Hub UI remains platform-branded at V1; tenant brand customisation is deferred beyond V1. The single V1 exception is the PDF Execution Summary export, which carries a basic tenant logo uploaded under platform control. Do not build a tenant theming surface in slice 4.

THE HUB'S BANNER REGION IS A CLOSED SET OF THREE CLASSES AT V1, all SoW Fact: the suspension banner (Tenant Admin only for soft and hard, all web users in compliance), the platform-support-session banner with its End-session control, and the platform-announcement banner. Slice 4 must build the banner region as a three-slot region and no more.

THE END-SESSION CONTROL IS A REAL CONTROL, NOT A NOTICE. MOD-DOH-13 makes it deliberately available to ANY signed-in tenant web user rather than only the Tenant Admin, with the stated reason that a session must not continue merely because one person is away. The banner is undismissable while the session is open, and the termination is itself an audited act recorded with its cause. Support session states: open, ended_by_time_box, ended_by_tenant, ended_by_engineer.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-13 FUNC-DOH-13-2.1.2 — all five roles except Worker

findings.claim: SUPPORT ACCESS IS READ-ONLY AT V1 and the compliance-emergency path is the only platform access class with write capability into tenant data. No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console. A compliance-emergency access produces a full post-session report to the tenant of what was accessed; that report is Allowed to the Tenant Admin and Read-only to the Read-only Auditor, and Unavailable to Supervisor, Quality Manager and Worker.

PLATFORM ANNOUNCEMENTS: the client's platform team may post an in-product banner at the top of the tenant Hub for a defined duration; it expires automatically. Announcement states: active, expired. Every tenant role is Explicitly prohibited from posting or editing one; all Hub web users see it; Workers do not (announcements render in the Hub).

TENANT-STATE FAILURE BEHAVIOUR IS PART OF THE SPINE AND MUST BE BUILT IN SLICE 4. Governed by FB-DOH-STATE-008. On a lost or delayed tenant-state transition event the Hub uses a state cache with an age check; beyond tolerance it applies the STRICTER of the last known state and the platform default, which for an unreadable state means treating master-data writes as blocked; if that fails it goes read-only with the completion pipeline preserved. Terminal safe state: the floor completes what it started and starts nothing new. Recovery is a fresh state read which lifts the precautionary restriction in the same act; reconciliation replays tenant_state_history and asserts the applied class matched the true state for every minute of the outage.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-01 FB-DOH-STATE-008 — every write path in slice 4

findings.claim: RECONNECT DISCIPLINE: on reconnection the Hub refetches tenant state BEFORE re-enabling any write control, so a tenant suspended during an outage is never permitted a write it should not have. Tenant state is read on every request and applied before any write control renders. Offline, the tier and usage view degrades to last loaded figures with a freshness marker under FB-DOH-CORE-001 and the upgrade/downgrade-request controls DISABLE rather than queue.

NO ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ANYWHERE IN THIS SPINE. No agent proposes, decides or applies a tier change, a suspension, a reactivation or an archival act; no agent opens, ends or records a platform access session. Both modules are fully functional with all agents paused. Agent behaviour is explicitly unchanged by a commercial suspension — coaching, deviation briefs and the shift handoff brief continue under soft and hard.

AUDIT TAXONOMY FOR MOD-DOH-01, enumerated: tier assignment and change; pending-downgrade creation, supersession and effect; every suspension entry and exit; reactivation; archival; export-on-archival production; pilot conversion; ladder-threshold crossings; and every precautionary restriction applied under FB-DOH-STATE-008 together with its lift. Audit entries commit in the same transaction as the action — an action that cannot be audited does not happen.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-11 consumer (slice 10) but the write is emitted from slice 4

findings.claim: TWO PERMANENTLY REJECTED AUTOMATIONS bind this spine and must not be built: P12 automatic tier downgrade when consumption fits ('Rejected. The source assigns this to a person. Technical feasibility is not a reason.'), and P13 automatic suspension release on payment ('Explicitly prohibited at V1'). Two do-not-use-cron controls also bind: DNC-18 compliance suspension entry and exit must never be a scheduled sweep, and DNC-13 suspension enforcement on a device must be the local cache-validity rule plus the command channel, never a server sweep.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-01 — no scheduler may execute a tier or suspension transition

findings.claim: THE TENANT-CONFIGURATION FLOOR RULE: a tenant may configure itself STRICTER than a matrix or default shows and NEVER looser, and the Tenant-Configuration Registry rejects a looser-than-floor value outright at the write with the bound stated, rather than accepting and logging it (DNC-22). This governs every settings screen SCR-DOH-026 exposes in slice 4.

THE HUB SCREEN INVENTORY the tenant lifecycle spine touches: SCR-DOH-002 Tier and usage read view (Read-only for Tenant Admin, Unavailable for Worker), SCR-DOH-003 Suspension status panel (Read-only), SCR-DOH-023 Platform Access History (Read-only for Tenant Admin and Read-only Auditor), SCR-DOH-026 Tenant administration settings register (Allowed with conditions — floors and ceilings enforced). The source states it does NOT enumerate a screen inventory, navigation structure or visual design; everything beyond the named screens is Derived Clarification and open to the client's design review.
findings.bindingOn: slice 4 screen build — treat the inventory as proposed, not frozen

findings.claim: REGULATED-INDUSTRY MODE IS A SECOND PLATFORM-SET ENTITLEMENT WITH A TENANT-SIDE READ FACE, and its role split DIFFERS from the tier view's. MOD-DOH-17 'View the tenant's mode status' is Read-only for Tenant Admin, Quality Manager AND Read-only Auditor, and Unavailable for Supervisor and Worker — whereas MOD-DOH-01's tier view is Read-only for Tenant Admin and Read-only Auditor only, with Quality Manager Unavailable. Build the two read faces separately; do not share one visibility rule.

THE SOURCE IS SILENT ON WHETHER A TIER UPGRADE IS AVAILABLE UNDER SOFT SUSPENSION. Soft suspension blocks 'all configuration edits including tenant settings'; a tier upgrade is a self-service Tenant Admin write. The soft-state blocked/open enumerations do not name tier change on either side, and SCR-DOH-SUSPEND-SOFT's disabled-actions list does not include it. For a state whose default trigger is non-payment this is a material gap. RECORD AS UNRESOLVED; do not infer either way.

THE SOURCE IS SILENT ON WHETHER THE END-SESSION CONTROL SURVIVES SUSPENSION. Under hard suspension 'everything else is read-only' and End-session is a write governed by FB-DOH-WRITE-002; under compliance suspension all logins are blocked so no tenant user can see the banner at all — yet SEQ-026 has the Hub 'mirror the access into the tenant's audit stream for the tenant to read ON REACTIVATION', which concedes the tenant is blind during the state. Neither module states whether the tenant retains its terminable-session guarantee while suspended.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-13 FUNC-DOH-13-2.1.2 under MOD-DOH-01 state gating

findings.claim: THE SOURCE IS SILENT ON RECERTIFICATION UNDER HARD SUSPENSION. Soft suspension explicitly keeps recertification of existing workers open, with the reason stated. The hard-state open enumeration does not name recertification or clearances at all — only step execution, capture, sync, substitution-to-complete, summaries, notifications and audit. A qualification expiring mid-hard-suspension therefore has no stated renewal path, only substitution. Slice 4 owns qualifications; flag this to the client rather than choosing.

THE SOURCE IS SILENT ON HOW AN ARCHIVED TENANT RETRIEVES ITS EXPORT. FUNC-DOH-01-3.1.2 says export-on-archival is produced at no charge with 'Roles allowed: Tenant Admin to retrieve; the client's platform team to produce', while SEQ-032 states the Tenant Admin LOSES WORKSPACE ACCESS AT ARCHIVAL and every other tenant role's access ends. No delivery channel outside the workspace is named.

THE SOURCE IS SILENT ON PRECEDENCE BETWEEN A TENANT-SPECIFIC OVERRIDE AND A TIER ENTITLEMENT (DEC-FEAT-004 records it as unstated), and on global-disable / tenant-override / tier-entitlement precedence generally (DEC-FEAT-003). The 14-step effective-control evaluation order answers both — but it is classified 'User-Mandated Product Extension', not SoW Fact, so it is a proposal, not a contract.

THE HUB IS ONLINE-ONLY. Every offline note in MOD-DOH-01 and MOD-DOH-12 resolves to FB-DOH-CORE-001 degrade-to-last-loaded-with-a-freshness-marker plus disabled write controls. Compliance device stops land at the device's NEXT CONTACT AND NEVER BEFORE, and the Hub never renders a device as stopped or locked until acknowledgement — the per-device position is rendered honestly, with unreached devices enumerated individually with last-seen times.
