contradictions: TENANT STATE SET — FIVE OR SIX. MOD-DOH-01's identity card and §4.2 give five states: active, soft_suspended, hard_suspended, compliance_suspended, archived (L26875, L3914). The OBJ-TENANT object card and the Super Admin console give SIX by adding 'pilot' as a lifecycle state: 'active, pilot, soft-suspended, hard-suspended, compliance-suspended, archived; transitions by the client's platform team' (L7643), restated at L4645 and L4649. Compounding it, §4.2.5 says a pilot tenant is 'functionally identical to a paying tenant' (L26971), which reads as pilot being a FLAG, not a state. Slice 4 must decide whether the Hub's state enum has five or six members and whether pilot is orthogonal; record BOTH readings.

TENANT STATE SET — THE PROVISIONING STATES ARE MISSING FROM BOTH ENUMERATIONS. SEQ-004 tenant creation moves the record 'draft' → 'awaiting administrator' → 'active' (L61336, L61340), and L75096 makes it a hard gate: 'A tenant record that has not completed every mandatory provisioning step remains in a safe draft state in which no user can authenticate, no operational data can be created, no device can enroll, and no work package can be generated.' Neither 'draft' nor 'awaiting administrator' appears in the MOD-DOH-01 five-state set (L26875) or the six-state OBJ-TENANT set (L7643). Slice 4 owns tenant setup, so it owns exactly the states nobody enumerated.

SOFT-SUSPENSION RELEASE — OPERATOR SIGNAL vs AUTOMATIC ON PAYMENT (DEC-SUSP-001, the most-repeated contradiction in the source). §4.2.4 says soft suspension lifts when the client's team clears the commercial hold and the platform acts on the operator's signal, NOT on a payment event; §4.2.1 and §8.12 say there is no payment integration (L26961, L26967, L26856). Against this, §8.9.2 gives the soft exit as 'Automatic on payment' and Part IX says 'soft clears on payment' (L4649, L113743). Adopted working position 2026-08-14: operator signal only, payment path left open and unbuilt — but it is classified 'Derived Clarification — adopted working position', NOT SoW Fact, and client ratification remains outstanding (L26967, L27070). Recurs at L2201, L3914, L7739, L13272, L21304, L41353, L81024, L94810, L96507, L101033, L111180.

THE WORKER-FACING COMPLIANCE MESSAGE EXISTS IN TWO WORDINGS, AND THE CONTRADICTION HAS TWO COMPETING DECISION IDENTIFIERS. §4.2.3 and §7.11: 'Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved.' §8.9.2: 'Operation suspended — your work has been saved.' The shorter form omits the only actionable instruction. Filed as DEC-MSG-001 at L5263, L44923 and L71249, and as DEC-SUSPMSG-001 at L114674, and at L100694 as 'proposed identifier not yet assigned in this chunk'. The message is declared 'quoted verbatim and fixed platform-wide' (L26931), so the divergence is build-blocking for a string that cannot be paraphrased.

THE SUPPORT-SESSION BANNER TEXT EXISTS IN TWO WORDINGS. §4.12.2 / MOD-DOH-13 / SB-DOH-025: 'Platform support is viewing your TENANT. Started [time]. Engineer [name]. End session.' (L29168, L29274). §8.15.1 / SCR-DOH-BANNER-01: 'Platform support is viewing your WORKSPACE...' (L9709, L14851, L16024). Recorded as a related divergence under DEC-MSG-001 at L5263. Both are given as the source's own words.

WHO MAY PRESS END-SESSION. MOD-DOH-13 says ANY signed-in tenant web user may end it — Supervisor, Quality Manager and Read-only Auditor are each 'Allowed with conditions — the control belongs to the tenant' — with the security rationale that a session must not continue because one person is away (L29199, L29272, AC-DOH-13-3 at L29286). Against this, the notification-matrix condition [N20] states the banner 'carries the End-session control, WHICH ONLY THE TENANT ADMIN MAY EXERCISE per FUNC-TEN-017 [SoW Fact — §8.15]' (L22780), and the controls register at L1476 and L99430 lists allowed_roles as Tenant Admin alone. This is a 4-role-vs-1-role difference on a security control.

DOES THE BANNER AND END-SESSION APPLY TO ALL THREE ACCESS CLASSES? DEC-EMEREND-001, explicitly Client Decision Required: §8.15.1 attaches the banner and the End-session control to the NORMAL SUPPORT SESSION only and says nothing about the compliance-emergency path or the JBS grant (L14870, L14878, L15504). MOD-DOH-13 nevertheless mirrors all three classes identically into Platform Access History (L29166, AC-DOH-13-1 at L29284). The recommendation on record is banner on all three, End-session on support and JBS but NOT on compliance-emergency — undecided, decision owner the client's legal and compliance owner.

HOW MANY SURFACES RENDER THE SUPPORT BANNER — ONE, THREE, OR FOUR. MOD-DOH-13 confines it to the Hub: it renders 'in the Hub's banner region defined in 19.1.6' and the Worker cell reads 'Not applicable — the banner is a Delivery Operations Hub web element' (L29189, L29198). §8.15.1 says 'a persistent strip across the top of EVERY TENANT SURFACE' (L14851). TEST-BOUND-1004 asserts the banner appears in 'all FOUR tenant web surfaces' (L14917) — but only three tenant surfaces are web, the fourth being native mobile. TEST-SUP-1404 asserts 'the THREE tenant web surfaces' (L16158). Four incompatible statements of banner reach.

DEVICE ENROLMENT AUTHORITY — TENANT SELF-SERVICE OR PLATFORM ACT (DEC-DEVOWN-001). AC-SA-13-02 and FUNC-SA-13-04-A1 are unambiguous: 'No console role can enroll a tenant's device; enrollment is tenant-self-service within platform policy', 'Allowed: Tenant Admin. Prohibited: every console role from enrolling', with TEST-SA-13-D2 asserting four console refusals (L45565, L45570). Against this, the SEQ-004 tenant landing screen disables 'Enrol a device' with 'Device enrolment is performed by the platform team from the Super Admin platform console' (L61357), and the soft-suspension storyboard disables it with 'Device enrolment is a platform action and is unavailable while the account is on hold' (L65039). Recorded as DEC-DEVOWN-001 at L8459 and L10324: §7.5.2 gives enrolment to Super Admin, §8.13.4 gives it to the tenant. Devices are slice 4; this is build-blocking.

DOES SOFT SUSPENSION BLOCK DEVICE ENROLMENT? §4.2.3's soft-state blocked list is stated 'exactly' and enumerates new Jobs, Workers, locations, shifts, parts and all configuration edits — device enrolment is NOT in it (L26919). SCR-DOH-SUSPEND-SOFT adds it as a disabled action anyway (L65039). Either the 'exactly' enumeration is incomplete or the storyboard over-blocks.

PENDING DOWNGRADE — AUTOMATIC OR MANUAL. AC-DOH-01-3 and §4.2.2 state a queued downgrade 'takes effect at the start of the first cycle in which consumption fits' and NOTIF-DOH-01-6 fires when it does (L26909, L27041, L27021) — an automatic execution. P12 in the rejected-automations register explicitly refuses it: 'P12 — Automatic tier downgrade when consumption fits ... Rejected. The source assigns this to a person. Technical feasibility is not a reason', and §8.9.3 is cited as 'executed only by the client's platform team, never mid-cycle' (L101422, L101447). Slice 4 must not implement an auto-executing downgrade without resolving this.

WHERE DOES TENANT SUSPENSION SIT IN THE AUTHORISATION ORDER — FIRST, SECOND, OR TWELFTH? The Chapter 17 policy-decision-point sequence evaluates, in order: 'tenant suspension state, role grant, object state, segregation of duties, and platform floor or invariant' — suspension FIRST of five, floor LAST (L20702). The six-rule matrix precedence states 'The platform floor beats the suspension rule beats the scope beats the object state beats the condition beats the cell' — suspension SECOND of six, floor first (L20841, L20862). The fourteen-step effective-control evaluation order places 'Tenant suspension state' at step TWELVE, after tier entitlement, tenant entitlement, tenant override and experimental cohort (L46550, L46556, L46560). The third is classified 'User-Mandated Product Extension', not SoW Fact. Three different answers to 'when do I check the suspension state'.

CAN A TENANT ARCHIVE FROM A SUSPENDED STATE? MOD-DOH-01's state diagram draws archival from Active only: 'Active --> Archived : tenant archival' (L26933-L26954). SEQ-032 requires the opposite: its precondition and starting state are STATE-TENANT-HARD-SUSPENDED, and 'The ending state STATE-TENANT-HARD-SUSPENDED becomes the starting state of SEQ-032' (L71252, L71268, L71270). The SEQ-031 object-state diagram likewise draws HardSuspended --> Offboarding and omits Compliance suspension entirely (L71218-L71237).

THE TIER AND USAGE VIEW HAS TWO OWNING MODULES AND FOUR SCREEN IDENTIFIERS. MOD-DOH-01's card says it 'feeds MOD-DOH-12 for the tenant read view' (L26877) and the screen is listed under MOD-DOH-01 as SCR-DOH-002 (L26053), as SB-DOH-013 (L27029), and as SCR-DOH-03 under 'MOD-DOH-01 FEAT-DOH-0101' (L48097); yet FUNC-DOH-12-3.2.1 renders the same five elements as a MOD-DOH-12 function with its own AC-DOH-12-6 and TEST-DOH-12-N2 (L29100, L29136, L29144). One screen, two modules, four identifiers, and a card that points at MOD-DOH-12 for 'the tenant read view' when the tenant view of platform administration is MOD-DOH-13.

THE TIER AND USAGE VIEW HAS FIVE ELEMENTS OR SEVEN. MOD-DOH-12's source status, AC-DOH-12-6, TEST-DOH-12-N2 and SB-DOH-013 all agree on five: meter definition, consumption against ceiling, ladder position with burst-band status, Active Locations at Site level, suspension status (L27029, L29136, L29144, L29154). The §4.11.5 summary row lists seven: 'its own ledger, tier, suspension status, meter definition, consumption, ladder position, and active-location count' (L4000). The ledger and the tier name itself are in one list and not the other.

THE USAGE LADDER HAS FOUR STATES OR FIVE. MOD-DOH-01: below_80, at_or_above_80, at_or_above_100_burst, above_125_flagged — four (L26875). §8.12's state row: 'ladder: below 80 · 80 · 100 · burst · above 125' — five, splitting the 100 crossing from the burst band (L4650). Since AC-DOH-01-9 requires the burst-entry event to be DISTINCT from the 100 percent escalation (L27047), the five-value reading may be the operative one.

THE HUB SCREEN-IDENTIFIER NAMESPACE IS NOT SINGLE-VALUED. The same surface carries SCR-DOH-001..026 (L26051-L26076), SCR-DOH-01/02/03 (L48095-L48097), SB-DOH-001/003/013/025 (L25591, L25757, L27029, L29274), and free-form identifiers SCR-DOH-SUSPEND-SOFT, SCR-DOH-SUSPEND-HARD, SCR-DOH-SUSPENSION, SCR-DOH-BANNER-01, SCR-DOH-TENADM-01, SCR-DOH-ONBOARD-MAP, SCR-DOH-ARCHIVECASCADE (L65028, L65152, L71241, L14851, L16455, L18024). The source itself states it never enumerates a screen inventory (L26045), so no namespace is authoritative.

IS COMPLIANCE SUSPENSION A PLATFORM-TEAM ACT OR A ROOT-APPROVED CRITICAL-CLASS ACT? §4.2.3's suspension table says compliance is 'initiated only by the client's platform team' (L26921) and MOD-DOH-01 says nothing about root approval anywhere. Elsewhere compliance suspension is named in the ten critical-class actions requiring Root Super Admin approval (L15360, L55942, L7643), and SEQ-026 shows Noah's submission creating 'no state change yet' until Aisha the root approves (L65270, L65271). The Hub's model of who caused a compliance transition is under-specified against the console's.

ANONYMISATION vs THE NO-PURGE MODEL, AND vs LEGAL HOLD. DEC-ANON-001 leaves confirmation that 24-month anonymisation stands unchanged under the no-purge model as an open drafting item, presumed yes (L26969, L44187). DEC-HOLDANON-001 / DEC-SEC-019 records that a legal hold is stated to suspend tiering and compliance-driven deletion but is NOT stated to suspend anonymisation — the one irreversible act, and exactly the attribution a hold exists to preserve (L97408, L104368). Both are unresolved on the platform's only irreversible operation.

'IMPERSONATION CONTROL' READS TWO WAYS (DEC-IMPERSONATE-001 / DEC-ACCESS-002). §4.12.4 lists 'cross-tenant visibility and impersonation control' among what the Hub must not carry (L29172), against four positive statements that support is read-only without exception, no ambient browsing exists, audit never records acting-as-role, and no role-escalation path exists (L17647, L104207). Reading A: it names the guardrail that PREVENTS impersonation. Reading B: it implies an impersonation feature and therefore a fourth access class, against a closed set of three. Slice 4's Platform Access History must render whichever the client confirms.

IS THE COMPLIANCE-EMERGENCY PATH REALLY THE ONLY WRITE PATH INTO TENANT DATA? §8.15.2 says it is (L14877, L29272), but §8.8.5 provisions onboarding implementation staff an author-and-submit role INSIDE the tenant workspace, and §8.8.5 contemplates JBS authoring capacity that writes (DEC-JBSWRITE-001 at L14877, DEC-ACCESS-001 at L104209). AC-DOH-13-4 makes 'support access is read-only at V1; no support-session action can write a tenant record' testable (L29287) — it does not cover the other two classes.

THE FIVE-ROLE MODEL IS UNDERCUT BY THREE UNRESOLVED ROLE DECISIONS THAT REACH SLICE 4. DEC-ROLE-001: §3.5 fixes five and denies a Quality Director, while §6.1.3 lists 'Plant Manager / Quality Director' as a user group and §5.18 lists Plant Manager in a table headed 'Fixed role' (L3813, L16284, L16730, L34967, L92125, L103449). DEC-PLUS-001: the matrices use 'Supervisor and above' and 'QM+' shorthand across five roles the source calls additive and NON-HIERARCHICAL (L34969, L98707, L99285, L109102). DEC-COUNT-001: the §1.7 numbers canon says '5 fixed roles' without qualifying them as tenant roles while Part VIII adds four console roles and the source states no combined figure (L118414, L118945). Every one of the 60 MOD-DOH-01 permission cells rests on a role set with three open decisions against it.

THE READ-ONLY AUDITOR'S TENANT-WIDE READ IS ASSERTED AND THEN CONTRADICTED. §4.8.1 grants read-only access across the tenant including the full audit log (L21852), which MOD-DOH-01 honours by giving the Auditor the same reads as the Tenant Admin (L26885, L26896). But DEC-AUDSTU-001 records the Studio role table omitting the Auditor entirely (L23065, L34742, L114693) and DEC-AUDEXPORT-001 records auditor export as unstated while report export is a Tenant Admin and Quality Manager capability (L16891). SCR-DOH-002's access column names only Tenant Admin and Worker and is silent on the Auditor (L26053).

THE HUB IS SIMULTANEOUSLY THE SYSTEM OF RECORD AND ORIGINATES NO OPERATIONAL DATA. 'The Delivery Operations Hub is the per-tenant operational system of record, yet no operational data originates in the Delivery Operations Hub itself — the Frontline Worker Application is the sole origin' (L1562). For slice 4 this bites on tenant setup: the Hub owns tenant, user, worker, qualification and device master data but is told it originates nothing.

USAGE-LEDGER EXPORT IS BOTH V1 AND V2 (DEC-USAGE-001). §8.7.1 places outbound data delivery in the second version, while §8.12.4 and §4.11.5 have export to the client's commercial systems existing at V1 and AC-SCOPE-062 requires the ledger to export in a form consumable by an external commercial system (L96587, L2798, L4650). The tenant-side face of the ledger is slice 4's; whether it exports is unresolved.

value.topic: SURF-DOH slice 4 cross-cutting spine: location hierarchy, shifts, the five tenant roles per-control, and Site/Area scoping

findings.claim: The location hierarchy has exactly three named levels in fixed order: Site (the facility) -> Area, also called Line (the functional zone where Jobs are scheduled) -> Location, also called Cell (the workstation). Both names are canonical; the source uses 'Area (Line)' and 'Location (Cell)' interchangeably with the bare terms.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-02 data model and every scope picker in slice 4

findings.claim: Depth is the tenant's choice, configured in the tenant administration area, not on the location screens themselves. A tenant may operate all three levels or a shallower structure. The depth value is a registry-governed setting bounded platform-side by the Super Admin tenant-configuration registry.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-02 + tenant administration area setting SCR-DOH-026

findings.claim: Hierarchy depth is settable before Jobs exist and constrained afterwards; the re-parent/level-change control is blocked outright while in-flight Jobs exist, with archive-and-recreate as the only sanctioned path. Refusal must name the blocking Jobs and write nothing.
The Site level is mandatory as the anchor for timezone and shifts, and the hierarchy is declared a platform-wide data-model contract that no surface may fork.

DEC-SITE-001 adopted working position (option c, adopted 2026-08-14): Site is mandatory AND the platform auto-creates one default Site at tenant provisioning. That Site is a real record with a real identifier, renameable by the Tenant Admin, never a hidden construct. Classification is 'Derived Clarification — adopted working position', explicitly never SoW Fact; client ratification is outstanding. Build to this.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-02 provisioning path and MOD-DOH-01 tenant creation

findings.claim: Site fields: name; address as plain text at V1; contact; timezone (exactly one per Site); status. Map and geocoding visualisation are deferred beyond V1 and render 'Not applicable' for all five roles.
Area fields: name; parent Site; status; bound Shifts. Area is the outer bound of the Supervisor's usual scope.

Location (Cell) fields: name; parent Area; required certification where the cell-narrowing model is used; status. The required-certification value is a gate input protected as configuration, not free-text metadata, and it narrows assignment without any per-worker-per-cell grant table. Below the Cell there is no further hierarchy level at V1.

Node lifecycle is two states plus two cascade states: node = active | archived; archival cascade = cascade_pending_reassignment | cascade_complete. The cascade states are Derived Clarification, not SoW Fact.

Archival cascade is a guarded loop that cannot be short-circuited: archiving a Site or Area enumerates every bound Job, auto-pauses each (no new runs, full history preserved), notifies the Tenant Admin with the list, and holds archival in cascade_pending_reassignment until every paused Job is reassigned or explicitly archived. The cascade cannot silently strand a standing Job.
Archived node semantics: no new Jobs or Workers bind to it; historical runs and Summaries remain accessible and exportable.

Timezone rule: exactly one timezone per Site; every Shift inherits it; per-Area and per-Shift overrides are deferred beyond V1 and are Explicitly prohibited for every role including the Tenant Admin. The Shift editor shows the inherited timezone as read-only text with no override control.
Active Locations are metered at Site level only, for the tenant's usage view. Computed, no role may edit.

Equipment is not a first-class entity at V1. Creating an equipment record is Explicitly prohibited for all five roles through the location, parts and Job paths; equipment is referenced only through Data Capture inside a step.

Named-location provenance (site, line, cell) is stamped into the runtime envelope of every capture and rendered to the tenant's configured depth. A rename in the Hub never retroactively renames provenance already captured; reconciliation is by identifier, never by name.

MOD-DOH-02 per-control matrix, 12 controls, all five roles explicit. Tenant Admin: view tree Allowed; create Site/Area/Location Allowed-with-conditions (blocked in soft, hard and compliance suspension); edit name/address/contact Allowed-with-conditions (any time, fully audited); re-parent or change levels Allowed-with-conditions (blocked while in-flight Jobs exist); split/merge/re-parent an Area Explicitly prohibited (unsupported at V1); archive Site or Area Allowed-with-conditions (cascade first); reassign a paused Job Allowed; set Site timezone Allowed-with-conditions; set a Location's required certification Allowed; map Not applicable; create equipment Explicitly prohibited.

MOD-DOH-02 non-admin cells: Supervisor and Quality Manager get 'Allowed with conditions — own Site and Area scopes' on View the location tree, and the Supervisor uniquely gets a WRITE: 'Reassign a paused Job during the cascade — Allowed with conditions, own Area scope'. Quality Manager, Read-only Auditor and Worker are Explicitly prohibited on that write. Worker is Unavailable on the tree entirely.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-02 — the only non-Tenant-Admin write on this module

findings.claim: Shift is a first-class entity, created, edited and archived by the Tenant Admin in the tenant administration area. It belongs to a Site (inheriting its timezone), binds to one or more Areas, and carries its own digest delivery time. Preconditions: at least one Site exists and the tenant is not in a suspension state blocking master-data writes.

Shift record fields, exhaustively: name; nominal start and end times; parent Site (timezone inherited); bound Areas; digest delivery time. There is no recurrence field, no days-of-week field, no rotation pattern and no shift-calendar object anywhere in the source. Shift patterns and calendars do not exist in this blueprint — this is silence, not a deferral statement.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-03 — do not invent a pattern engine

findings.claim: A Shift anchors exactly three platform mechanics named as such in §4.3.5: the Worker-Shift consumption meter, the production_date rule for runs crossing midnight, and on-shift escalation resolution. Two further dependents are stated separately: per-shift digest scheduling, and the denormalised shift_id carried on the Run record.

Editing a Shift is forward-effective only. Completed runs are never re-stamped: their production_date, denormalised shift_id and Worker-Shift attribution stay as recorded. The denormalisation on Run exists precisely to make this true.

Shift lifecycle is two states: active, archived. Archival is refused while runs are scheduled against it — but that constraint is explicitly Derived Clarification, NOT SoW Fact, and the Supervisor must first cancel or reschedule those runs.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-03 — flag as derived before building the block

findings.claim: Per-shift digest: one digest service, one occurrence per Shift at its configured time, default 06:00, which is the source's stated solution to rolling shift starts without per-user scheduling. Recipients are all users with digest-eligible content in that Shift's scope. Users mute sections, never services.

MOD-DOH-03 per-control matrix, 7 controls. Tenant Admin: create Allowed-with-conditions (blocked in EVERY suspension state); edit Allowed-with-conditions; archive Allowed-with-conditions; bind to Areas Allowed; set digest delivery time Allowed (default 06:00); override inherited timezone Explicitly prohibited; view Allowed. All four other roles are Explicitly prohibited on all six write controls. View Shifts: Supervisor and Quality Manager Allowed-with-conditions within own scopes, Read-only Auditor Read-only, Worker 'Allowed with conditions — own assigned shift only'.

A shift bounds what a role may do through exactly ONE mechanism, and it is not a permission gate: escalation-target resolution. The Hub resolves the routed role against the roster of role-holders currently on shift at the Location; all on-shift holders are notified; the first acknowledgement claims the item. Where the roster is empty, delivery falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift and is visibly marked as a fallback with the original target's miss recorded. No permission cell anywhere in the blueprint is conditioned on the actor being on shift.

The second shift-bounded rule is the clearance escalation: a second clearance in the same AREA on the same SHIFT routes to the Quality Manager regardless of which worker it concerns. The escalation scope is deliberately Area-level, not per-worker, because repeated exceptions in one Area are a signal about the Area.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-04 clearance routing — needs Shift + Area context at grant time

findings.claim: There is no on-call calendar at V1. It is an explicit roadmap defined extension, listed alongside custom roles and delegation. Roles are resolved to people on shift at runtime by the Hub, with no rota object.

MAJOR GAP: the source never states how a person becomes 'on shift'. The Shift's stated outputs include 'the on-shift roster used by escalation resolution' and the Worker column of MOD-DOH-03 reads 'own assigned shift only', both of which presuppose a person-to-Shift binding — but no Shift input field, no worker-record field, and no control anywhere creates that binding. The Shift's inputs are name, times, parent Site, bound Areas and digest time only. Slice 4 must raise this as a decision; do not invent a roster mechanism.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-03 + MOD-DOH-04 worker record — blocking design question

findings.claim: There are exactly five tenant roles at V1 with fixed identifiers and remits: Tenant Admin ROLE-TEN-ADMIN (configuration, users and roles, the tenant administration area, tier and usage read view); Supervisor ROLE-TEN-SUP (worker records and qualifications, Job creation, run creation and scheduling, assignment and substitution, expired-certification clearances); Quality Manager ROLE-TEN-QM (Job approval, Summary review, the Anomaly Register, never-held clearances, run cancellation anywhere, the Qualification Calendar); Read-only Auditor ROLE-TEN-AUD (read-only across the tenant including the full audit log); Worker ROLE-TEN-WKR (executes runs on the Frontline app; sees own record and own certification alerts).
There is no Quality Director role and Job Owner is a field on the Job record, not a role. Custom roles are deferred beyond V1 and creating one is Explicitly prohibited for all five roles.

Scopes are exactly three orthogonal dimensions held simultaneously: Tenant, Site, Area. Location (Cell)-, Job- and worker-level scoping are deferred beyond V1, so no rule may depend on them; attempting such a grant is Explicitly prohibited for every role.

Scope restriction mechanics on lists: FUNC-DOH-09-2.2.2 applies the scope filter to every list, filter, search and export in the Hub, automatic, no role may bypass. The filter is applied to CACHED content too, so a stale Hub view cannot leak out-of-scope data. Area-scoped Supervisors cannot see nodes outside their scope in any list, filter, search or export.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-09 FEAT-DOH-09-2 — enforce server-side, per request

findings.claim: What a role sees outside its scope, exactly: nothing, and the refusal must not disclose that the object exists. Evaluation step 4 refuses a scope miss without disclosing the out-of-scope object; SCR-DOH-DENY-01 renders 'This record is outside your assigned Site and Area scope' WITHOUT naming the record, and offers the 'Why was I refused' view SCR-DOH-ROLE-04, which itself never reveals the existence of out-of-scope records. AC-ACCESS-1007 is the assertion.

Access is an intersection of nine conditions, all of which must say yes; role permission is only condition 1 and assigned scope is condition 2. Two precedence rules sit above the intersection: explicit deny wins, and safety controls win even over a root-level allow. Evaluation order is safety first, then role, then scope, then entitlement.

A scope miss returns the status token 'Unavailable', owned by the Tenant Admin, per the nine-condition owner table. That is distinct from 'Explicitly prohibited', which is a role-permission or safety refusal. Slice 4 must not blur the two: Unavailable means a future release could surface it, Explicitly prohibited means it must never be surfaced without changing a platform rule.

MOD-DOH-09 per-control matrix, 12 controls. Tenant Admin: create/edit user Allowed-with-conditions (blocked in every suspension state); assign or remove role Allowed-with-conditions (mandatory-role rules enforced); assign or remove scope Allowed; configure single sign-on Allowed; issue or reset a managed PIN Allowed; view the user and role register Allowed. Five rows are Explicitly prohibited for ALL FIVE roles including Tenant Admin: remove the last Tenant Admin; remove the last approver-capable role while a Job exists; create a custom role; delegate a role temporarily; scope a permission to a Location, Job or worker; plus 'act as another role in the audit trail'.

MOD-DOH-09 non-admin cells: Supervisor gets 'Issue or reset a managed personal identification number — Allowed with conditions, own scope, for workers' (the only non-Tenant-Admin write in this module) and 'View the user and role register — Read-only, own scope'. Quality Manager gets Read-only own scope on the register only. Read-only Auditor Read-only. Worker Unavailable on the register.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-09 — Supervisor PIN reset is a real slice-4 write path

findings.claim: Two-track login. Track 1: single sign-on by SAML and OpenID Connect, available on ALL tiers, for staff and administrative roles. Track 2: platform-managed username plus personal identification number for hourly floor workers, set up in-platform with no burden on the tenant's identity provider. Staff with no identity provider use the same managed-credential path. Cached mobile credentials remain valid offline for the tenant-set offline credential-trust window, default ~24 hours, platform ceiling 72 hours.

Multi-role is additive: permissions are the union of held roles. The audit log records the user identity and the action and contains NO acting-as-role field; introducing a role-assumption record is Explicitly prohibited. Delegation is deferred beyond V1 and cover is achieved only by manually adding then removing a role, both audited.

Two mandatory-role rules enforced at the moment of removal (the only moment they can be violated): at least one Tenant Admin always exists, and an approver-capable role must exist whenever a Job exists. The role-assignment screen renders both as permanent statements, not post-save validation messages.

Permission resolution runs per request; a role or scope change takes effect on the next request without a sign-out. The permission system FAILS CLOSED: an unresolvable permission denies the request, the denial names the outage and offers no bypass, and no request is served on a cached permission decision.
User states are closed: User = active | suspended_by_tenant_state | archived. Role assignment = assigned | removed.

Suspension state overrides every permission matrix, and is reading rule 5 of section 17.1. Soft: master-data writes blocked while operations continue, banner to Tenant Admin only. Hard: everything read-only except the enumerated completion pipeline. Compliance: all logins blocked. Every slice-4 write control (locations, shifts, users) is a master-data or configuration write and therefore dies under soft suspension.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-02/03/04/09 write guard — inherited from MOD-DOH-01

findings.claim: Permission matrix status vocabulary is a closed set of nine tokens and only these nine, lint-enforced by TEST-RBAC-101. A blank cell is a build-blocking defect of the same class as a missing specification limit.

Hiding a control is not security: the UI renders a control only where the policy decision point would permit the action, and the policy decision point denies regardless of what the UI rendered. Both must be generated from ONE configuration source (AC-RBAC-003 is written as a generation requirement, not a consistency requirement); a divergence event is a release-blocking defect, not a monitored tolerance.
findings.bindingOn: slice 4 UI + API — single source of authorisation config

findings.claim: Unenumerated functions inherit their parent module cell from MTX-TEN-02a, narrowed by object state, the prohibition matrix and the identity's Tenant/Site/Area scopes. No inherited status may be broader than its parent module cell, and any function touching a platform floor may never be inherited and must be enumerated explicitly.

MOD-DOH-04 per-control matrix (slice-4 qualification spine), 15 controls. Notable: Enter a qualification — Tenant Admin Allowed, Supervisor Allowed with full audit, Quality Manager Explicitly prohibited, Worker Explicitly prohibited (self-attestation not permitted). Grant clearance for an expired certification — Tenant Admin Explicitly prohibited, Supervisor Allowed-with-conditions (mandatory categorised reason: Emergency cover, Training-in-progress, or Other; QM notified on grant), Quality Manager Allowed. Never-held clearance — Supervisor Explicitly prohibited, Quality Manager only. Create/edit worker record, recertify, back-date, archive, reactivate and bulk import are all Supervisor 'own scope'.

Qualifications carry per-Area scope on every record, and a worker may hold qualifications for Areas across multiple Sites of the tenant. This is the point where the location hierarchy feeds the gate, so Area identity must be stable before qualifications are entered.

The qualification gate is the ONLY configurable gate on the platform. Two postures: strict (platform default, hard blocks lifted only by clearance) and notify-only, which is the platform floor — no silent posture exists and no tenant setting may weaken the gate below it. Setting the posture or the clearance duration is Tenant Admin only, in the tenant administration area.

MOD-DOH-14 Qualification Calendar per-control matrix: open the Calendar — Tenant Admin Read-only, Supervisor 'Read-only, filtered to own Area scope', Quality Manager 'Allowed, tenant-wide', Read-only Auditor Read-only, Worker Unavailable. The 60-day horizon is fixed and changing it is Explicitly prohibited for all five roles. There is no Calendar export — Not applicable for every role, because the SoW does not specify one.

Tenant administration area settings that slice 4 owns, with defaults and bounds: qualification-gate posture (default strict blocking); clearance duration (numeric default TBD — Client Decision Required); offline trust window (~24h, ceiling 72h); clock-skew threshold (~5 min, ceiling 60 min); digest composition and per-shift delivery times (06:00 per shift); hierarchy depth (Site/Area/Location, Site always present); shift definitions (tenant-created objects, no numeric bound). The tenant may configure stricter than the platform floor and NEVER looser; the registry REJECTS a looser-than-floor value rather than accepting and logging it.
The tenant administration area is a screen group inside the Delivery Operations Hub, NOT a sixth surface. The platform has exactly five surfaces and no sixth.

Setup order is fixed by the worked sequences: SEQ-006 configures hierarchy, shifts and settings (Tenant Admin only, no other role account exists yet), and only then SEQ-007 creates people, because Site, Area, Location and Shift must exist so that Site and Area scopes can be assigned. Slice 4 cannot invert this.

Scope-assignment validation stated in the sequence: 'an assigned Area must exist under an assigned Site'. This is a real constraint on the scope picker, and it is in tension with the 'orthogonal, held simultaneously' framing — see contradictions.

Prohibited at account creation, stated explicitly: creating a role that is not one of the five; delegating a role temporarily; creating a Tenant Super Admin, which does not exist; granting any tenant user platform-console authority. A denied attempt to create a sixth role is refused and audited with no account created.

There is NO device module on SURF-DOH. The nineteen-module Hub inventory contains no device entity; device enrollment, mode, de-authorisation, wipe and device policy live on the Super Admin platform console (§8.13), and device state reaches the tenant only through the command channel. If slice 4 is scoped to include 'devices', that scope has no Hub module to build against.
findings.bindingOn: slice 4 scope boundary — raise before building

findings.claim: Artificial intelligence touches none of this spine: no agent creates, edits, archives or proposes a location change; no agent creates, edits or archives a Shift; no agent creates users, assigns roles or grants scopes, and AI may never elevate its permissions, change tenant scope or impersonate a role. All three modules are fully functional with agents paused.

Offline posture for this spine on the Hub itself: reads degrade under FB-DOH-CORE-001 with the scope filter STILL applied to cached content; every structural and configuration write control disables; no location, shift or permission write is ever queued client-side, so reconnection requires no reconciliation of pending edits.

Audit weight: every Shift creation, edit, Area-binding change, digest-time change and archival is audited at the same weight as a permission change, because Shifts drive escalation resolution and the consumption meter. Every location node creation, edit, REFUSED structural change (recorded as an attempt), archival request, auto-pause, reassignment and completion is audited. Every permission change records acting identity, affected identity, the role or scope changed, and before-and-after values, committed in one transaction with the action.

DEC-PERM-001 is BLOCKING for MOD-DOH-09 and unresolved: the source never states whether permission is computed per role-scope PAIR or as the union of roles crossed with the union of scopes. The two computations give different answers for a user holding Quality Manager at Site scope on one plant and Supervisor at Area scope on another. Recommendation is Option A (per pair), which requires scope to be stored per ROLE ASSIGNMENT rather than per user — a data-model consequence that must be settled before the permission model is built. Owner: JBS engineering lead ratified by the client's product owner.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-09 data model — decide before slice 4 schema is frozen

findings.claim: DEC-SHIFT-001 is BLOCKING for MOD-DOH-03 and unresolved: shift-to-Area cardinality is unanswered on three axes — one Shift to many Areas, one Area to many Shifts, and whether two Shifts bound to the same Area may overlap in time. Recommendation is Option A (many-to-many with an explicit overlap validation), because overlapping shifts on one Area make the Worker-Shift meter ambiguous and metering is commercially visible. Owner: the client's product owner.

DEC-SCHED-003 is blocking for the scheduler and unresolved: daylight-saving semantics for shift-anchored schedules are not specified — two hours a year are absent or duplicated in every observing timezone. Recommendation is a split rule: nominal local time for wall-clock schedules such as the 06:00 digest, elapsed-time-from-shift-start for schedules defined relative to a shift boundary, with each schedule definition declaring which family it belongs to.

DEC-NOSHIFT-001 remains Client Decision Required and unresolved: the nobody-on-shift escalation fallback default (Quality Manager irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery) is carried in the source as an open drafting value, not a settled rule. DEC-QMNONE-001 sits behind it — the source is silent on what happens when the Quality Manager role has no holder at all.

DEC-WKRVIEW-001 is unresolved and directly governs slice 4: whether the Worker's own-record and own-certification view is a Hub surface or a Frontline module. Until decided, the build serves the own-record view on the Frontline Worker Application ONLY and DENIES Hub access to the Worker role, naming the decision in the denial. MTX-TEN-01's Hub/Worker cell and MTX-TEN-02a's MOD-DOH-04/Worker cell both read Client Decision Required. This decides whether hourly floor workers need web accounts at all.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-04 and MOD-DOH-09 — Worker has NO Hub session in slice 4

findings.claim: DEC-AUDROLE-001 is unresolved: combining Read-only Auditor with any acting role produces an identity that is not read-only, which defeats the role's entire purpose under the additive model. Recommendation is to PROHIBIT the combination at assignment. Slice 4's role-assignment guard has no source-backed rule here.

DEC-PLUS-001 is unresolved: the source's authority matrices use 'Supervisor+' and 'QM+' without defining an ordering across five additive, non-hierarchical roles. Chapter 19 handles it by enumerating every cell by role with no plus form; read any surviving plus form as role-set membership, never as a hierarchy.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-09 — never implement a role hierarchy

findings.claim: DEC-ROLE-001 is unresolved: §3.5/§4.8.1 fix five roles and deny a Quality Director, while §6.1.3 lists 'Plant Manager / Quality Director' as a Command Center user group and §5.18 lists Plant Manager under a heading reading 'Fixed role'. The build proceeds on the five-role reading; Plant Manager and quality engineer are personas layered on the five, the latter via the Studio authoring grant.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-09 role table — five columns only

findings.claim: MOD-DOH-02, 03 and 09 are all Band A. Band labels are internal build-sequencing lenses with no commercial or acceptance meaning; both bands are V1 and the scope is signed as A plus B together. No acceptance criterion may be conditioned on band membership.

closedSets.name: Login tracks
members: Single sign-on by SAML or OpenID Connect (staff and administrative roles, all tiers)
Platform-managed username plus personal identification number (hourly floor workers, and staff with no identity provider)

closedSets.name: Mandatory-role rules
members: At least one Tenant Admin always exists
An approver-capable role must exist whenever a Job exists

closedSets.name: Shift-anchored platform mechanics (as named in section 4.3.5)
members: production_date rule for runs crossing midnight

closedSets.name: Qualification expiry alert stages (tenants may add earlier stages, never remove or delay one)
Hub banner classes
members: Suspension banner (Tenant Admin only in soft and hard; all web users in compliance)
Platform-support-session banner with its End-session control
Platform-announcement banner posted by the client's platform team

contradictions: MOD-DOH-02 Supervisor status disagrees between layers. MTX-TEN-02a gives the Supervisor 'Read-only' on the whole Location Configuration module (L22008), but the module's own per-control matrix gives the Supervisor a WRITE: 'Reassign a paused Job during the cascade — Allowed with conditions, own Area scope' (L27123), and FUNC-DOH-02-2.2.2 names 'Tenant Admin and Area-scoped Supervisor for reassignment' (L27171). Under section 17.4.3's inheritance rule no status may exceed its parent module cell (L22149), so one of the two is a defect. Both readings recorded.

MOD-DOH-03 Worker status disagrees between layers. MTX-TEN-02a gives the Worker 'Unavailable' on Shift Management (L22009); the module's per-control matrix gives the Worker 'View Shifts — Allowed with conditions, own assigned shift only' (L27297). A cell cannot be broader than its parent module cell (L22149). Both readings recorded.

MOD-DOH-09 Supervisor and Quality Manager statuses disagree between layers. MTX-TEN-02a gives both 'Unavailable' on Permissions, Roles and Access (L22015); the module's per-control matrix gives the Supervisor 'Issue or reset a managed personal identification number — Allowed with conditions, own scope, for workers' (L28531) and gives both Supervisor and Quality Manager 'View the user and role register — Read-only, own scope' (L28532). Both readings recorded.

Who may ENTER a qualification is stated three different ways. 19.6's per-control matrix: Tenant Admin 'Allowed', Supervisor 'Allowed', Quality Manager 'Explicitly prohibited' (L27472). MTX-TEN-03 FEAT-TEN-QUAL-ENTER: Tenant Admin 'Unavailable' [J13 'qualifications are supervisor-entered'], Supervisor and Quality Manager both 'Allowed with conditions' (L22163). MTX-TEN-02a condition [H4] says the Tenant Admin holds identity administration while 'qualification entry itself is supervisor-entered' (L22027). MOD-DOH-14 then calls it 'a Supervisor and Tenant Admin act' (L29348). Four passages, three different answers on the Tenant Admin and two on the Quality Manager. All recorded; none picked.

Who may grant an EXPIRED-certification clearance disagrees on the Tenant Admin token. 19.6 gives Tenant Admin 'Explicitly prohibited' (L27476); MTX-TEN-03 FEAT-TEN-CLEAR-EXPIRED gives Tenant Admin 'Unavailable' (L22164). The two tokens are explicitly not interchangeable per L20825. Both recorded.

'Refused, not filtered' versus 'scope filter on every list'. AC-ARCH-002 and the architecture chapter state that a request outside scope is REFUSED rather than filtered (L10717, L10814). MOD-DOH-09 FUNC-DOH-09-2.2.2 states that the scope filter is applied to every list, filter, search and export in the Hub, and to cached content as well (L28580, L28596), and MOD-DOH-02 Security says out-of-scope nodes cannot appear in any list, filter, search or export (L27212). Slice 4 must decide which mechanism governs collection endpoints; both statements are on the record.

Scope orthogonality versus scope nesting. Section 4.8.2 and MOD-DOH-09 state Tenant, Site and Area as three ORTHOGONAL dimensions held simultaneously (L28491, L14516). SEQ-007's validation states 'an assigned Area must exist under an assigned Site' (L67486), which is a nesting rule — and yet SEQ-007 step 1 then creates Sam with the Supervisor role scoped to AREA-ASSY-A alone, with no Site scope assigned (L67494), while the Chapter 10 example describes Sam as holding Site scope on Riverside Plant AND Area scope on Assembly Line A separately (L14215). Three incompatible readings of whether an Area grant requires a Site grant.

Quality Manager scope is both tenant-wide and Area-filtered. Condition [U3] gives the Quality Manager 'Tenant scope for review, the Anomaly Register, and run cancellation anywhere' (L21933) and [H12] repeats 'run cancellation anywhere' (L22029); section 21.1.2 states that a Quality Manager's decision queues are filtered to the Areas in their grant and that a gate item raised in an Area they do not hold is not visible to them (L35027). Both recorded; this is exactly the ambiguity DEC-PERM-001 raises and does not resolve.

Two incompatible screen registers cover the same slice-4 screens with clashing identifiers. Chapter 19 register: SCR-DOH-004 Location hierarchy browser, SCR-DOH-005 Site/Area/Location detail and edit, SCR-DOH-006 Shift register and Shift editor, SCR-DOH-019 Users, roles and scopes (L26054, L26055, L26056, L26069). Chapter 27 register: SCR-DOH-04 Location hierarchy configuration, SCR-DOH-05 Shift management, SCR-DOH-18 Users, roles and scopes (L48098, L48099, L48112). The two-digit and three-digit schemes collide (SCR-DOH-04 vs SCR-DOH-004) and the module-to-screen mapping differs. Both recorded.

Two incompatible feature-identifier schemes for the same modules. Chapter 19 uses FEAT-DOH-02-1 / SUB-DOH-02-1.1 / FUNC-DOH-02-1.1.1 style (L27159 onward, L27317 onward, L28574 onward); Chapter 27's screen register uses FEAT-DOH-0401 / FEAT-DOH-0903 / FEAT-DOH-0101 style (L48095, L48097, L48101). Chapter 11 uses a third, FUNC-DOH-02010001 / FUNC-DOH-03010001 / FUNC-DOH-09010002 / FUNC-DOH-09020001 (L16483). Three identifier grammars for the same slice-4 functions. All recorded.

Parts Registry openers disagree. SCR-DOH-025 lists the Tenant Admin as the only role (L26075); SCR-DOH-06 lists 'Tenant Admin, Supervisor' (L48100); MTX-TEN-02a MOD-DOH-19 gives the Quality Manager 'Allowed with conditions' [H34] for the Studio inline-add seam (L22025). Both recorded.

Qualification Calendar openers disagree, and the source admits silence. SCR-DOH-010 names the Quality Manager (L26060); SCR-DOH-09 names 'Quality Manager, Supervisor, Read-only Auditor' (L48103); condition [H27] states plainly that Supervisor visibility is 'Not specified in the Statement of Work' and offers only a recommendation with no decision identifier raised (L22042); 19.16's control matrix nonetheless states Supervisor 'Read-only — filtered to own Area scope' as if settled (L29345). The Supervisor's Calendar access is an unrecorded gap presented as a decided cell.

Location (Cell) archival is asserted in one place and flagged as an assumption in another. OBJ-008 states the Cell is 'archived through the same soft path' (L7839); the object-chapter source status states that the Location (Cell) archival cascade treatment is an ASSUMPTION requiring confirmation because the source states the cascade for Sites and Areas only (L7961). Meanwhile MOD-DOH-02's per-control matrix offers only 'Archive a Site or Area' with no Cell control at all (L27122). Both recorded; slice 4 has no source-backed Cell archival control.

Concurrent-edit conflict policy contradicts the platform's own last-write-wins prohibition. SEQ-007 states that two Tenant Admins editing one user record 'resolve last write wins with both writes audited' (L67506); the seam chapter states that no silent last-write-wins is permitted on a record type with a single named producer and that last-write-wins is unsafe wherever clocks are unreliable (L2308). Both recorded.

DEC-SITE-001 preserves two live readings of the same rule: section 2.1 marks Site-as-required-minimum an open drafting item recorded as recommended rather than settled, while section 4.3.1 states plainly that 'The Site level is mandatory'. Part XII carries it as an open drafting value. The adopted working position (mandatory + auto-created default Site) is Derived Clarification, never SoW Fact, and client ratification is outstanding (L27082, L112932, L27237).

DEC-AREA-001 preserves two live readings that bite on hierarchy depth: section 2.1 says the old 'one Area per Job' constraint becomes 'one parent node per Job' at the tenant's configured depth, while section 4.5.1 says a Job carries its single Area binding as a hard constraint. They differ materially for any tenant that configures Location (Cell) depth. The adopted position is section 2.1's. Slice 4 does not own Jobs, but it owns the depth setting that makes the difference visible (L6892, L6982, L7831, L47225).

value.topic: SURF-DOH slice 4 cross-cutting spine — Worker records, Qualifications, the qualification gate, clearances, the Qualification Calendar, and the support-not-surveillance prohibitions (MOD-DOH-04 primary, MOD-DOH-14 secondary, MOD-DOH-09 seam)

findings.claim: MOD-DOH-04 'Worker Lifecycle and Qualifications' is the owning module of the whole spine. Its canonical chapter is 19.6 at lines 27447-27637. It is a Band A module, source-anchored at SoW §4.4 through §4.4.9, §2.8, §3.6, §4.8.3. Nine separate module identity cards for MOD-DOH-04 exist across the blueprint with DIFFERENT purpose strings and DIFFERENT roles_allowed lists — treat 27447 as governing and the rest as derived restatements.

MOD-DOH-14 Qualification Calendar is a separate Band A/B module (chapter 19.16, lines 29312-29444) that is a READ-ONLY PROJECTION of OBJ-DOH-QUAL and OBJ-DOH-WORKER. It holds no state of its own, has no write capability of any kind (AC-DOH-14-4), and its unavailability affects NO enforcement anywhere (AC-DOH-14-5). Objects affected = 'None'.

WORKER vs USER — the load-bearing passage is §13.1 'The identity vocabulary — fifteen terms that are not synonyms' at line 17462. The spine is stated as a one-way ladder at 17472-17483 and drawn at 17485-17498: Persona -> User -> Account -> Role type -> Scope -> Grant -> Effective permission set -> Session -> Audit entry. Qualification and Temporary grant enter the effective set FROM THE SIDE, never through the role chain.
findings.bindingOn: slice 4 identity data model; MOD-DOH-04 / MOD-DOH-09 seam

findings.claim: The single sentence that settles the Worker/User distinction: 'an expired certification blocks execution without touching login, and a clearance restores execution without touching the role' (line 17500). Restated normatively at step 7 of the identity workflow: 'Qualifications ... gate execution, not access' (line 17480), and in Transition table B: TRN-QUAL-04 current-session effect = 'None; the person can still log in' (line 17503 / 19503).
findings.bindingOn: authorization service — qualification checks must not sit in the session/permission resolver

findings.claim: They are two distinct objects with distinct identifiers, distinct owners and distinct create authorities. OBJ-028 / OBJ-WORKER 'Worker record' = 'the operational record of a person who executes work on the floor', created by a SUPERVISOR, owned by MOD-DOH-04 (§4.4.1). OBJ-027 'User account' = the authentication identity, created by a TENANT ADMIN, owned by MOD-DOH-09 (§4.8). OBJ-WORKER's key_relationships explicitly include OBJ-USER.
findings.bindingOn: slice 4 schema — OBJ-DOH-WORKER and OBJ-027 are separate tables joined by an identity link

findings.claim: The worker record carries an 'identity link' as a FIELD — i.e. the link to the account is a property of the worker record, not an identity. Full field list at 8367: identity link; worker_type label; instruction-difficulty profile; language preference; qualifications by reference; status.

A worker record can exist WITHOUT a credential. WF-WKR-001 happy path step 4: after the record commits 'the worker becomes eligible for credential issuance, role assignment, and qualification entry' — three separate downstream capabilities. Its reconciliation explicitly 'lists incomplete worker records and workers with no credential'. The diagram at 52807-52814 shows the record as a gate to three separate downstream capabilities.

Supervisor CAN create/edit a worker record (Allowed with conditions, own scope) but is Explicitly prohibited on User account, Role grant and Scope grant. This is the operational proof that the two records are separate. Tenant Admin holds the account side; Supervisor holds the worker side.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-04 write authority vs MOD-DOH-09 write authority

findings.claim: 'Worker' is ALSO one of the five fixed tenant ROLE types (ROLE-TEN-WKR) — so the word carries three distinct meanings the implementation must keep apart: the role type, the worker record object, and the person. The role table at 17513 lists Role type as row 1 and User as row 2 precisely to force this separation.
findings.bindingOn: slice 4 naming — do not collapse ROLE-TEN-WKR with OBJ-DOH-WORKER

findings.claim: Worker record states: active, archived, reactivated — 3 states, Supervisor authority, with re-validation prompted on reactivation 'so that nothing is silently re-trusted'. NO deletion path exists at any point in the source.

Two-step departure is mandatory and ORDERED: (1) reassign all active and upcoming runs, (2) then archive. Open step executions close as abandoned with the recorded reason 'Worker departed.' FUNC-DOH-04-1.1.3 states 'Online: enforced in order.' Offline devices holding the departed worker's run receive the reassignment command at next sync; until then the Hub renders it as queued.
findings.bindingOn: departure flow on SCR-DOH-007 / worker record Activity region

findings.claim: Re-employment reactivates the PRIOR record with history intact plus a MANDATORY re-validation prompt asking which prior qualifications still apply. AC-DOH-04-11: 'nothing is silently re-trusted'.

findings.claim: The instruction-difficulty profile is a CLOSED three-value field — simple, standard, expanded — maintained by Tenant Admin or Supervisor, NEVER by the worker. AC-WF-WKR-001-03 states the field 'accepts only simple, standard, or expanded'. On invalid value the platform MUST NOT silently default: the record is held incomplete and CANNOT RECEIVE ASSIGNMENTS ('no assignment is safer than an assignment whose instructions may render at the wrong level').

Qualification record fields (OBJ-031): worker reference; certification type; per-Area scope (which may span Areas across MULTIPLE SITES of the tenant); certification date; entry date; expiry date; recertification lineage. findings.claim: Entry date is recorded AUTOMATICALLY by the platform; certification date is user-supplied.
