TEST-WF-WKR-006-03 asserts no apparent gap appears in the record VIEW.

Recertification hard rule: the new expiry MUST postdate the old. A recertification whose new expiry does not postdate the previous is REFUSED with the rule stated. Recording a renewal LIFTS ACTIVE BLOCKS IMMEDIATELY server-side, delivered at the device's next sync.

THE GATE — the qualification gate is 'the only configurable gate on the platform'; the specification gates and the evaluation gate are hard and non-configurable. Its only configurable dimensions are the enforcement POSTURE and the CLEARANCE DURATION.
findings.bindingOn: tenant administration area — gate posture + clearance duration settings

findings.claim: Two postures only: STRICT (the platform default) and NOTIFY-ONLY. Notify-only is the PLATFORM FLOOR — 'no silent posture exists, and no tenant setting can weaken the gate below it'. Only the Tenant Admin may select, in the tenant administration area. TEST-DOH-04-D4: attempt a posture weaker than notify-only, assert rejection NAMING THE FLOOR and assert nothing is written.

The gate validates at exactly THREE moments: at assignment, at run start, and at override-carrying screens. 'A single bypass at any one point does not open the gate.' Note the wording diverges: line 1525 says 'gated screens' where 1548, 8423, 19444, 24028, 28214 and 53789 say 'override-carrying screens'.
findings.bindingOn: three separate enforcement call sites — assignment service, run-start, device step gate

findings.claim: At-expiry rule, strict posture, quoted rather than paraphrased at 27427: re-assignment to runs requiring the expired certification is blocked; the worker MAY COMPLETE THE ENTIRE CURRENT RUN, the block applying only after that run ends; THERE IS NO GRACE PERIOD BEYOND IT; enforcement lands at STEP LEVEL on the mobile device with the enforcement state delivered over the command channel at sync.
findings.bindingOn: expiry enforcement — server assignment block + on-device step gate

findings.claim: Under notify-only there is NO BLOCK TO CLEAR. Assignment and execution proceed; the same events raise IMMEDIATE notifications to Supervisor AND Quality Manager and are fully flagged in the audit trail AND the Execution Summary. An expired qualification nonetheless remains a STANDING SIGNAL in the Client Command Center until resolved, whichever posture the tenant runs.
findings.bindingOn: NOTIF-DOH-04-7; Execution Summary flag; CC standing signal

findings.claim: Enforcement is LOCAL and DETERMINISTIC. 'The device enforces from its pinned package; a gate block encountered offline parks the run.' The gate is evaluated on-device from packaged rules, so an offline device blocks correctly without the network. 'No agent enters, edits, clears or expires a qualification' and 'the qualification gate is deterministic and lives on the device' — the whole module functions unchanged with agents paused.

NO NOTIFICATION IN THIS MODULE IS THE ENFORCEMENT. Stated verbatim at 27586: 'The enforcement is the server-side assignment block and the on-device step-level gate.' Corollary at 2681: 'A notification must never be the only mechanism enforcing a gate, and here it is not: the gate itself is local and remains closed.'

Expiry warning schedule: 14, 7, 1 and 0 days — FIXED. Tenants MAY ADD earlier warnings and MAY NEVER remove or delay a stage. FUNC-DOH-04-2.2.1 roles: 'none — automatic; the Tenant Admin may add earlier stages. Roles prohibited: all, for removing or delaying a stage.' TEST-DOH-04-... / TEST-15-29 asserts removal of the 7-day stage is refused. The Super Admin console 'holds the platform floor for the warning schedule at 14, 7, 1 and 0 days and rejects any tenant attempt to widen it.'
findings.bindingOn: expiry sweep scheduler; MOD-DOH-10 baseline (slice 10) but the schedule is slice 4 data

findings.claim: The four stages have EXACTLY SPECIFIED, DIFFERENT audiences per stage — this is why the source models them as four distinct STATES rather than notifications hung off one state (27533). Supervisor AND Tenant Admin receive each stage direct (NOTIF-DOH-04-1); the Quality Manager receives the expiry picture inside the PER-SHIFT DIGEST only (NOTIF-DOH-04-2); the worker is alerted for their OWN certifications only (NOTIF-DOH-04-3).
Qualification expiry is part of the MANDATORY NOTIFICATION BASELINE and always fires; it cannot be disabled (§4.9.2).
findings.bindingOn: notification preference UI — expiry rows must be non-configurable

findings.claim: Escalation on the expiry event: the Supervisor is notified IMMEDIATELY; if unacknowledged within a CONFIGURABLE window, DEFAULT 2 MINUTES, it escalates to the Quality Manager. Escalation resolves against the roster of role-holders CURRENTLY ON SHIFT, platform-wide. Where nobody holding the target role is on shift, the platform falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role IRRESPECTIVE OF SHIFT and marks the delivery as a FALLBACK so the gap is visible rather than silent. This no-shift default is carried unresolved as DEC-NOSHIFT-001.
findings.bindingOn: NOTIF-DOH-04-4; MOD-DOH-03 on-shift roster dependency; DEC-NOSHIFT-001

findings.claim: MOD-DOH-04 depends on MOD-DOH-03 (Shift Management) purely for on-shift roster resolution, and on MOD-DOH-02 (Location Configuration) for Area scope. Both are slice 4. Preconditions: at least one Site AND Area must exist before per-Area qualification scope can be set.
findings.bindingOn: slice 4 build order — MOD-DOH-02 and MOD-DOH-03 precede MOD-DOH-04

findings.claim: A CLEARANCE is 'the sanctioned, audited exception to a qualification block — the platform's replacement for the informal override'. The HUB owns the clearance record and its enforcement; the GRANTING ACT is Client Command Center action number 10. It is written with its audit entry IN ONE TRANSACTION, in the audit log AND on the worker's qualification record.
findings.bindingOn: clearance service — Hub-owned record, CC-invoked action

findings.claim: Three clearance situations with distinct granting authorities, CLOSED at the table on line 27431-27434. (1) Expired certification -> SUPERVISOR, mandatory categorised reason, QM notified on grant. (2) Never-held qualification -> QUALITY MANAGER, authorisation required in addition to the reason code; Supervisor Explicitly prohibited. (3) Second clearance in the same Area on the same shift, REGARDLESS OF WORKER -> routes to the Quality Manager.

The second-clearance escalation scope is DELIBERATELY AREA-LEVEL, NOT PER-WORKER: 'repeated exceptions in one Area are a signal about the Area.' This is a support-not-surveillance rule dressed as an escalation rule and MUST NOT be re-keyed per worker. AC-DOH-04-7 and TEST-DOH-04-D3 both assert routing occurs for a DIFFERENT worker under the same Supervisor. Enforcement is server-side and 'therefore unaffected by device state'.
findings.bindingOn: second-clearance routing — key on (Area, Shift), never on (Worker)

findings.claim: Clearance reason codes are a CLOSED categorised set of three — Emergency cover, Training-in-progress, Other — plus optional free text. Mandatory on grant.

Clearance duration is a TENANT SETTING, explicitly 'not a fixed per-shift expiry' and 'uniform at tenant level and deliberately not per user'. The clearance LAPSES AUTOMATICALLY at the end of that duration and the lapse is recorded. 'Roles prohibited: all, for extending a clearance beyond its duration without a fresh grant.'

A LAPSED CLEARANCE RETURNS THE QUALIFICATION TO EXPIRED, NEVER TO VALID. Stated as the crucial modelling decision at 27533 and 19486: 'a clearance can never quietly become a permanent qualification' / 'Modelling it any other way would let a chain of clearances silently substitute for recertification.' AC-DOH-04-8, AC-15-33, TEST-DOH-04-N3, TEST-15-26 all assert it.
findings.bindingOn: clearance lapse handler — must restore Expired state

findings.claim: Clearance metadata is fully specified and IMMUTABLE after grant: who granted, for whom, where, why, when granted, when lapsed. 'Editors are nobody after grant.' 'Roles prohibited: all, for editing a recorded clearance.' The corpus is QUERYABLE FROM THE SUPER ADMIN PLATFORM CONSOLE to detect patterns across time.

Offline clearance behaviour is fully specified: a gate block encountered offline PARKS the run; the worker CONTINUES OTHER ASSIGNED RUNS; the parked run resumes only when the clearance ARRIVES AND IS APPLIED on the device. The Hub must render the clearance as QUEUED, NEVER AS APPLIED. AC-DOH-04-13 and TEST-DOH-04-O1 assert this.
findings.bindingOn: command channel rendering on SCR-DOH-008 and the device

findings.claim: A lapse that occurs while the device is OFFLINE is enforced BY THE DEVICE from the clearance's CARRIED DURATION — 'the device does not need to be told a clearance ended.' Bounded by the offline trust window. TEST-DOH-04-O2 asserts it.
findings.bindingOn: device clearance cache — carry duration, not an end event

findings.claim: HUB-SIDE OFFLINE RULE, easy to get wrong: qualification and clearance write controls DISABLE rather than QUEUE, 'because a queued clearance would be a safety control with no audit entry.' Reads degrade under FB-DOH-CORE-001.

Self-attestation is prohibited ABSOLUTELY and by CONSTRUCTION, not by permission check: 'no worker-role path reaches qualification entry' and 'the worker cannot reach this control'. AC-DOH-04-1 and TEST-DOH-04-D1 require the refusal to hold through EVERY path including the mobile application and any API.
findings.bindingOn: qualification entry — no worker-role route may exist at any layer

findings.claim: The anti-self-attestation check is by IDENTITY, not only by role: the platform 'checks that expiry postdates certification date AND THAT SAM IS NOT THE SUBJECT' before storing.

Supervisor permission ALONE authorises worker-record changes — 'the audit trail, not a second approval, is the control.' This is flagged as a DELIBERATE design decision 'stated in the source and should be understood as such at audit'. Do not add a second-approval step.
findings.bindingOn: worker-record write path — single-authority + audit, no maker-checker

findings.claim: Every qualification entry, every recertification WITH BOTH DATES, every clearance grant, use and lapse, every permission-relevant worker-record change, every departure and reactivation, and every import outcome is audited, COMMITTED WITH THE ACTION (one transaction).
findings.bindingOn: one-transaction audit guarantee on every MOD-DOH-04 write

findings.claim: THE QUALIFICATION CALENDAR: fixed 60-day forward horizon, TENANT-WIDE, Quality-Manager-owned, grouped and filterable by exactly four dimensions — week, Area, certification type, worker — each row linking through to the worker record. The horizon is NOT configurable: 'Change the 60-day horizon' is Explicitly prohibited for every role including Tenant Admin.

The Calendar's stated purpose is PLANNING, deliberately distinct from the alert ladder's ENFORCEMENT-ADJACENT purpose: 'it exists so recertification is planned against the schedule rather than discovered at the 14-day alert.' Two independent paths run off the same qualification data and neither replaces the other.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-14 design intent — do not merge with the alert ladder

findings.claim: Calendar role scoping: Quality Manager = Allowed, TENANT-WIDE. Tenant Admin / Read-only Auditor = Read-only. Supervisor = Read-only FILTERED TO OWN AREA SCOPE. Worker = UNAVAILABLE (TEST-DOH-14-D1 asserts refusal). Recording a recertification FROM the Calendar is Explicitly prohibited for the Quality Manager — 'qualification entry is a Supervisor and Tenant Admin act'.

Calendar edge case explicitly handled: a certification with NO EXPIRY DATE does not appear on the Calendar at all, and 'its absence is explained on screen rather than left as a silent omission'. Classified Derived Clarification. TEST-DOH-14-N1 seeds 5/30/59/60/61 days and asserts the boundary.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-DOH-14 projection query and empty-state copy

findings.claim: Calendar EXPORT is 'Not specified in the Statement of Work' and is recorded as such rather than invented — an explicit non-feature for every role. Do not build one in slice 4.
THE WORKER-BLOCKED RULES, enumerated. (1) Expiry under strict posture blocks NEW ASSIGNMENT to runs requiring that certification; current run completes; no grace period.

Worker-blocked rule (2): NO GATE CAN BE OVERRIDDEN BY THE WORKER IT BLOCKS. 'There is no on-device worker override' (§7.13.1). Stated across every Worker role card in the blueprint. TEST-DOH-04-D1 and TEST-15-25 assert refusal on EVERY surface.
findings.bindingOn: device Run Player block panel — no bypass control may exist

findings.claim: Worker-blocked rule (3): the block panel copy is specified. SB-15-06 — a gated step whose qualification has expired renders a block panel naming the certification, the expiry date, and exactly TWO paths: 'Ask your supervisor for a clearance' or 'Continue with your other assigned runs', with the run visibly marked Parked. 'The panel never offers a way past the gate.' Under notify-only it renders instead as a NON-BLOCKING notice with the same information.

Worker-blocked rule (4): the Hub-side banner copy is specified verbatim in SB-DOH-016 — a red banner above the worker record when any qualification is expired reading 'One certification has expired. New assignment to runs requiring it is blocked. The current run may be completed.'

Worker-blocked rule (5), SOFT SUSPENSION: creating a NEW worker is blocked as a master-data write, while RECERTIFICATION OF EXISTING WORKERS STAYS OPEN. Encoded in the matrix ('blocked for new workers in soft suspension') and in FUNC-DOH-04-1.1.1 / 2.1.2. TEST-TENADM-1708 asserts four refusals plus a successful recertification.
findings.bindingOn: suspension guard on MOD-DOH-04 writes — must discriminate create vs recertify

findings.claim: Worker-blocked rule (6), HARD SUSPENSION: every surface read-only except the enumerated completion pipeline — in-flight runs complete, capture, sync, compute summaries, close; NO NEW RUNS. Workers see nothing on mobile in soft or hard state.

Worker-blocked rule (7), COMPLIANCE SUSPENSION: all logins blocked immediately, in-flight runs STOP, devices lock at next contact with the fixed verbatim worker-facing message. Two wordings of that message exist in the source (see contradictions).

Worker-blocked rule (8), OFFLINE TRUST WINDOW: cached credentials, roles, scopes, qualifications AND clearances remain valid offline only for the tenant-set window, default approximately 24 hours, PLATFORM CEILING 72 HOURS. Beyond it the device forces re-sync and BLOCKS NEW WORK rather than trusting cached credentials. TRN-OFF-02: a worker mid-step when the window lapses COMPLETES THE STEP — the restriction applies to NEW RUN STARTS, not work in progress.
findings.bindingOn: offline authorization — restriction scope is new run starts only

findings.claim: Worker-blocked rule (9): a worker record with an INVALID instruction-difficulty value is held incomplete and CANNOT RECEIVE ASSIGNMENTS. Fail-closed by design.

MID-SHIFT LAPSE FALLBACK, primary contract — FAIL-15-05 'a qualification expires mid-shift and no supervisor is available to grant a clearance'. First fallback: the supervisor is notified immediately through the standard escalation path (Command Center alert plus email) and DECIDES REMOTELY — 'the supervisor does not need to be physically present'. Fallback failure: unacknowledged within the 2-minute window, escalates to the Quality Manager. Terminal safe state: THE RUN PARKS, the worker continues their other assigned runs, 'no work is done under an expired certification, and NO CLEARANCE IS GRANTED AUTOMATICALLY BECAUSE NOBODY WAS AVAILABLE'. Recovery: clearance granted, OR a qualified substitute assigned with a structured handover, OR the run cancelled with a categorised reason.
findings.bindingOn: mid-shift lapse handling — three named recovery routes, no auto-grant

findings.claim: Mid-shift fallback, module-level (FB-DOH-CMD-003, 'the highest-criticality pattern in this chapter'): failure = a clearance that cannot reach a device while a run is parked. (1) continued ordered queuing, run stays parked, Hub renders the clearance as QUEUED NEVER AS APPLIED. (2) authorised human escalation to the on-shift Supervisor and Quality Manager, who may REASSIGN the run to a qualified worker — 'a Hub-side act needing no device delivery' — or attend physically. (3) fallback-of-fallback: a CONTROLLED HOLD in which the Hub blocks further assignment of gated work TO THAT DEVICE. Terminal safe state: run stays parked, worker continues other assigned runs.

Mid-shift fallback, sweep failure (FB-DOH-SCHED-010): backfill against the ORIGINAL DUE TIME. Because expiry is evaluated at assignment AND at step level rather than only by the sweep, 'a missed alert delays a warning but NEVER PERMITS GATED WORK'. TEST-DOH-04-F2 asserts this.
findings.bindingOn: expiry sweep — enforcement must not depend on the sweep

findings.claim: Mid-shift fallback, blocked-and-no-response (§3.3 level): the platform default escalates to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, MARKED AS A FALLBACK DELIVERY — carried as DEC-NOSHIFT-001 and 'not treated as settled'. 'The run stays parked; it is NEVER RELEASED BY TIMEOUT.' A tenant asking for a worker-side override to keep the line moving is REFUSED.
findings.bindingOn: parked-run lifecycle — no timeout release path

findings.claim: Mid-shift reconciliation contract: reconciliation asserts that EVERY qualification whose expiry date has passed is in the expired state OR covered by an ACTIVE clearance, and REPORTS every exception rather than auto-correcting. TEST-DOH-04-R2 asserts exceptions are reported rather than auto-corrected. A parallel reconciliation lists parked runs with their age and reports clearances that lapsed while a run was still parked.

SUPPORT-NOT-SURVEILLANCE, the canonical section is 3.3 at lines 1994-2048, sourced to §7.1.2, §6.4.2, §7.7.6, §7.1.4, §7.1.5, §10.2, §5.16.1, §8.4.1. The governing statement: the application 'must be felt by the worker as support, not surveillance — a tool that helps them do the job right, not an instrument watching them for mistakes'. It is enforced by THREE concrete prohibitions plus ONE data-handling rule.
findings.bindingOn: every slice 4 screen and every downstream consumer of slice 4 data

findings.claim: PROHIBITION ONE — no worker-facing pace, EVER. 'No pace figure, no timer against expectation, no comparison to others, IN ANY MODULE, ANY STATE, ANY RELEASE OF THIS SCOPE'. Timing thresholds may drive coaching, but what the worker sees is support content, never the stopwatch. Restated at 2044 (AC-GOAL-030), 1548 (AC-PROD-031), 100651, 101497 (business rule 3), and as an absolute-target-of-zero indicator at 2375.
findings.bindingOn: AC-GOAL-030 / AC-PROD-031 / AC-SCHED-251 — full-screen sweep test TEST-GOAL-030, TEST-PROD-031, TEST-SCHED-251-01

findings.claim: PROHIBITION TWO — the oversight board is exception-led, NEVER a surveillance wall. The default Client Command Center board shows CELLS AND LINES, never individual workers. Worker-level detail appears ONLY on drill, opened from an exception, a pushed alert, or an approval item — 'never as a default wall of per-worker feeds'. The source gives three reasons: a per-worker live wall would promise a per-second feed the offline-first design cannot keep; it would carry disproportionate sync load; and it would create surveillance-wall optics that poison floor adoption.

PROHIBITION THREE — the app is scoped to the logged-in identity's own work. NO OTHER WORKER'S DATA APPEARS IN THE FRONTLINE APPLICATION AT ALL. Local storage holds ONLY the logged-in identity's own data, never any other worker's. The worker also never sees or resolves a sync conflict.

THE DATA-HANDLING RULE — the platform holds worker-level data as PURPOSE-BOUND AGGREGATES (qualification state, readiness flags, trends), NOT raw per-worker behavioural feeds. The profile memory store carries aggregate operator and asset patterns AS AGGREGATES ONLY, with a personal-information-redaction policy applied.

The resolution of the attribution-versus-presentation tension, stated rather than smoothed: complete attribution is required for auditability; minimal worker-level exposure is required for adoption. The source separates ATTRIBUTION IN THE RECORD from PRESENTATION IN THE INTERFACE — 'the envelope always carries who did what, and the interfaces refuse to render that as a performance display.' The two prohibitions in the §3.3 diagram are refusals OF PRESENTATION, not of recording. Classified Derived Clarification from §7.2.1, §6.4.2 and §7.7.6 read together.
findings.bindingOn: slice 4 read models — attribute fully, render never as performance

findings.claim: THE TWO ABSOLUTE RULES, stated at 101472 with no exception, configuration, tier gate or override: (1) 'Audit events must never become hidden employee surveillance.' (2) 'Artificial intelligence must never automatically make a disciplinary or employment decision.' They bind every scheduled process and every AI capability on the platform.
findings.bindingOn: platform-wide; enforced in slice 4 by the read-model shape

findings.claim: §45A.15 codifies the eight surveillance business rules at 101495-101502. Rule 1: the audit log's purpose is FIXED AT CREATION and may not be repurposed — 'an audit record proves what happened to a record; it does not authorise a report about a person's performance.' Rule 2: NO SCHEDULED PROCESS MAY CREATE, MATERIALISE OR PERSIST A PER-WORKER BEHAVIOURAL FEED, TIME SERIES OR RANKING. Rule 5: worker-level detail on drill only. Rule 7: AI is advisory and may never make a disciplinary or employment decision, nor be the input to one without human review, context and a right of correction.
findings.bindingOn: every persisted table and every scheduled job touching worker identity

findings.claim: The governing distinction table at 101482-101491 answers two questions explicitly for BOTH the immutable activity audit AND productivity analytics: 'May it be used for a performance judgement about a named individual?' -> Explicitly prohibited (audit) / Explicitly prohibited at individual level (analytics). 'May artificial intelligence read it and produce a conclusion about a person?' -> Explicitly prohibited for BOTH.
findings.bindingOn: audit read paths and analytics read paths

findings.claim: M-A4 Qualification state and readiness flags — the register entry that governs slice 4 directly. Individual-level measurement is ALLOWED here, uniquely and legitimately, 'because qualification is a property of a person and a safety control'. But PROHIBITED USES are named: 'using expiry frequency as a performance measure.' AI 'may flag readiness gaps; may not decide assignment.' AC-SCHED-253: 'Qualification state is per-worker, warned on the fixed schedule, and NEVER USED AS A PERFORMANCE MEASURE.'

M-A5 Clearance and override frequency — individual-level is EXPLICITLY PROHIBITED; 'the source's own framing is BY ROLE'. Prohibited uses: 'per-worker cut, per-worker ranking'. Bias risk 'high if re-cut per worker, which is why it is prohibited'. Context statement to hold onto: 'frequent clearances usually indicate a certification-planning failure, not a worker failure.' AI 'may propose a Lane-B change to qualification planning; MAY NOT NAME A WORKER AS A CAUSE.' AC-SCHED-254: the clearance-frequency data set is cut BY ROLE AND BY AREA, NEVER BY WORKER.
findings.bindingOn: clearance corpus queries; MOD-DOH-18 data set 4 (slice 6) reads slice 4 data

findings.claim: M-A1 Step-execution telemetry — attribution to the performing worker is REQUIRED for traceability, but individual-level PERFORMANCE COMPARISON is Explicitly prohibited. Prohibited uses named: 'ranking workers, disciplinary input, pay or shift allocation, any worker-facing display.' The reason is stated as a design fact, not a preference: 'a slow step may reflect downtime, a missing part, an unavailable approver, poor connectivity, or rework; none of these is visible in the raw number, WHICH IS PRECISELY WHY THE NUMBER IS NOT A PERFORMANCE MEASURE.' Bias risk 'high — comparing a worker on a difficult unit against a worker on an easy one is meaningless.'
findings.bindingOn: AC-SCHED-250; TEST-SCHED-250-01 (four refusal paths + audit row per attempt)

findings.claim: M-A2 Pace state per run — SUPERVISOR-ONLY, explicitly; pace is a property of THE RUN, not of a worker. Individual-level Explicitly prohibited as a per-worker measure. Prohibited uses: 'any per-worker aggregation, any worker-facing rendering, any automated consequence.' Pace triggers NOTHING by itself, and carries a platform default margin of 15% set per workflow.

M-A3 Coaching activations and dismissals — 'the most surveillance-adjacent signal on the platform; THE DEFAULT SILENCE IS THE CONTROL.' Individual-level Explicitly prohibited as a standing per-worker feed — 'the pattern is the signal, not the person.' Interventions are silent to the supervisor by default, escalating only on the Studio-defined repeated-coaching pattern. Prohibited use: 'counting dismissals per worker as a compliance metric.' 'Treating dismissals as non-compliance would be a serious misreading.' A dismissal is 'a learning and visibility signal, never a disciplinary signal.'

M-A6 Run no-show and lateness signals — 'the highest bias risk on this register'. Individual-level Explicitly prohibited AS AN ACCUMULATED MEASURE; 'no scheduled process may accumulate no-show counts per worker.' Worker transparency line worth quoting to the team: 'the worker is not notified of a no-show signal about themselves, because THE PLATFORM DOES NOT TELL WORKERS THEY ARE BEING COUNTED — IT DOES NOT COUNT THEM.' Prohibited uses: 'any per-worker no-show tally, any input to scheduling preference, any disciplinary use.' 'No artificial-intelligence involvement at all is permitted in this measure.'

M-A7 Worker-Shift consumption — per-worker BY CONSTRUCTION but it is 'a BILLING COUNT, NOT A BEHAVIOURAL MEASURE', consumed only as a tenant total. The per-worker granularity exists ONLY inside the ledger; the exposed figure is the tenant total. Prohibited uses: 'any productivity or attendance interpretation.' Bias risk 'severe if re-cut as shifts worked per person for any purpose other than billing, which is prohibited.'
findings.bindingOn: AC-SCHED-256 — Worker-Shift ledger must expose tenant totals only

findings.claim: M-A8 Immutable activity audit itself — prohibited uses named exhaustively: 'performance review, disciplinary evidence assembled by query, ranking, any export whose purpose is employee assessment.' AI 'may not mine the audit log to produce conclusions about individuals.' AC-SCHED-257 requires audit-log ACCESS to itself be audited, carry a named purpose, and the log's permitted purpose to be DISPLAYED wherever it is read.

M-A9 Emerging-pattern watch items — the subject is THE SCREEN, individual-level Explicitly prohibited. Prohibited use: 'naming workers in a watch item.' AC-SCHED-258: watch items never name a worker. The storyboard example is instructive: 'Screen 7 of Assembly — Wheel Bolt Torque Verification: 14 coaching activations across 6 runs this week.' No names.

M-A10 Any proposed per-worker productivity analytic — 'Purpose: NONE THAT SURVIVES THIS SECTION. Verdict: Explicitly prohibited at V1.' Any future proposal is a scope decision requiring an explicit client decision, a worker-transparency plan, a bias assessment, a human-review process and an appeal route — recorded as DEC-SCHED-009.

findings.claim: AC-SCHED-259 is the broadest AI prohibition and covers SUITABILITY INFERENCE explicitly: 'No artificial-intelligence component produces an output whose stated or implied subject is an individual worker's PERFORMANCE, CONDUCT OR SUITABILITY.' contradictions: QUALIFICATION STATE VOCABULARY — FOUR INCOMPATIBLE SETS, all describing OBJ-QUALIFICATION. (a) MOD-DOH-04 identity card, line 27460: valid, warning_14, warning_7, warning_1, expired, RENEWED (6). (b) MOD-DOH-04 mermaid diagram 27 lines later, lines 27515-27531: Valid, Warning14, Warning7, Warning1, Expired, CLEARED (6) — same module, same chapter, sixth member differs. (c) OBJ-QUALIFICATION extract at line 3720: valid, expiring, expired, cleared (4). (d) OBJ-031 lifecycle states at line 8425: valid, expiring, expired, RECERTIFIED (4). Nothing in the source reconciles them. Record all four; slice 4 must pick one and label it Derived Clarification (state names are explicitly Derived Clarification per line 27636).

SUSPENDED AND REVOKED QUALIFICATION STATES EXIST IN ONLY ONE PLACE. §15.5 (lines 19446-19470) models a ten-state machine including Suspended (TRN-QUAL-07, 'suspended by a supervisor with a recorded reason') and Revoked (TRN-QUAL-08, 'permanently withdrawn'), each with transition, effect, notification, audit and failure rows at 19507, 19508, 19520, 19521. MOD-DOH-04's identity card, features, functions, acceptance criteria and tests contain NO suspension or revocation path at all. Either §15.5 invents two states or chapter 19.6 omits two required transitions — the source does not say which.

CLEARANCE STATE SET — TWO INCOMPATIBLE SETS. MOD-DOH-04 identity card line 27460: granted, active, lapsed, superseded_by_renewal (4). OBJ-032 line 8445: requested (where applicable), granted, delivered, in force, lapsed (5). 'superseded_by_renewal' appears only in the card; 'requested', 'delivered' and 'in force' appear only in the object card. The delivery-state distinction is load-bearing because the Hub must render a clearance as queued and never as applied (line 27566).

WORKER RECORD STATE SET — TWO READINGS. Three states (active, archived, reactivated) at lines 3720, 8370 and 27460; TWO states (active, archived) at line 22389 in the OBJ-WORKER card of another chapter; and 'none, active' at line 61474. Whether 'reactivated' is a persisted state or a transition event is not stated anywhere.

WHO MAY ENTER A QUALIFICATION — DIRECT ROLE CONTRADICTION. MOD-DOH-04's roles-and-permissions matrix, line 27472: 'Enter a qualification | Tenant Admin: Allowed | Supervisor: Allowed — with full audit'. The SEQ-008 role table, line 67606: 'Tenant Admin | Read-only | Receives every expiry stage; DOES NOT ENTER QUALIFICATIONS.' Line 29348 sides with the first ('qualification entry is a Supervisor and Tenant Admin act'); the module purpose strings at 3707 and 25960 describe qualifications as 'supervisor-entered' throughout. Both readings are in the source.

WHO ISSUES A WORKER CREDENTIAL. WF-WKR-002 at line 52824 names 'Primary Supervisor or Tenant Admin' as the actor for credential issuance, and places the workflow inside MOD-DOH-04. The MOD-DOH-09 role rules at lines 10346 and 28522 make the Supervisor 'Explicitly prohibited' on User account. If credential issuance is a user-account act, the two statements cannot both hold. WF-WKR-002 itself is flagged Derived Clarification under DEC-INVITE-001 and its soft-suspension split is labelled 'Assumption' at line 52825, so the source knows it is on thin ice here.

WHO CREATES THE 'USER'. §13.1 step 2, line 17475: 'A Tenant Admin creates a USER record for that person in the Delivery Operations Hub surface, MODULE 9.' §4.4.1 / MOD-DOH-04 and WF-WKR-001 at lines 8363, 27470 and 52792: a SUPERVISOR creates the WORKER record in module 4. The §13.1 vocabulary table then gives, as its example of the term 'User', 'Maya Rivera, WORKER RECORD with an instruction-difficulty profile field' cited to §4.4.1 (line 17514) — collapsing the two objects it exists to separate. Whether 'user' and 'worker record' are one object or two is therefore ambiguous in the very section that defines the distinction.

DEC-WKRVIEW-001 — WHICH SURFACE RENDERS A WORKER'S OWN RECORD, UNRESOLVED. Reading one: the Worker 'sees own record and own certification alerts' inside the Hub role table [§4.8.1], and MOD-DOH-04's matrix grants 'Allowed with conditions — own record only' at line 27471. Reading two: Hub primary users exclude Workers [§1.2] and workers meet platform content exclusively through the Frontline surface [§5.18, Part VII]. The MTX-TEN-02a cell for MOD-DOH-04's Worker column reads 'Client Decision Required' at line 22010. Lines 23067, 20746. Blocking for slice 4 because it decides whether floor workers need web accounts at all.

DEC-NOSHIFT-001 — THE NO-ONE-ON-SHIFT ESCALATION DEFAULT IS UNRESOLVED. Escalation resolves against on-shift role-holders only, platform-wide; where nobody holding the target role is on shift the platform falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery. The blueprint carries this as 'an open drafting default' and 'not treated as settled'. Lines 2681, 27429, 27409, 19508, 52999.

DEC-SCHED-009 IS CITED FOR TWO UNRELATED SUBJECTS. At Card SCHED-029 (line 99444) and 98628 it is the DRIFT-CANARY CADENCE decision. At 101611, 103058 and 103153 it is the WORKER-PRIVACY decision — whether any individual-level productivity measurement is ever permitted, the minimum-population suppression threshold, and the client's employment-data policy. It is also cited at 10121 for backfill approval authority and at 104731/104734 for scheduler misfire policy. The extract flags this collision at line 99444. One identifier, at least three unrelated decisions.

THE NO-WORKER-FACING-PACE RULE HAS TWO CLASSIFICATIONS. §3.3 and §45A.15 classify it SoW Fact at §7.7.6 and §7.4 (lines 2002, 2032, 2048, 101497, 101613). A prohibition the team must implement absolutely is contractually classified two different ways.
